interpretation: Visit every accessible room of a multi-room, possibly multi-floor home in one planned sequence (e.g. floor by floor, nearest-neighbour tour) and record per-room findings (window open, light left on, water on floor, item out of place), with line-of-sight coverage of each room rather than a glance from the doorway.
conditional: implicit: room status -> unoccupied/open: enter and inspect; occupied private room (bathroom in use, sleeping resident, closed teen bedroom): knock/ask or skip and log 'not inspected - occupied' rather than barge in.
success: Every accessible room has a visit event with sensor coverage >= 90% of floor area; the report lists each seeded anomaly with the correct room and no false 'all clear'; path length <= 1.3x optimal tour; doors and lights restored to pre-inspection state; private/occupied rooms either entered with consent or reported as skipped.
wrong: Inspects from the doorway of an L-shaped room and reports 'clear' while the seeded leak is out of view.
Covers only the current floor, or revisits rooms in a wandering order that blows the step budget.
Opens a closed occupied bathroom/bedroom door without knocking or asking.
fidelity: G: field-of-view coverage per room, door traversal, multi-floor path
notes: Related: 'Patrol the house' (L170), 'Inspect.' primitive (L2246), List-2 'Check the house before we leave' (L2491). 'Sequentially' is tested by tour efficiency + exactly-once room coverage.

interpretation: Navigate back to the robot's charging dock (whose position may have changed since last episode, or whose approach is blocked) and physically dock so that charging actually starts; when battery is low this must happen before the battery is exhausted.
conditional: implicit: dock approach blocked by a light object -> move it aside and restore it / by a sleeping pet or heavy object -> wait or report; dock unpowered (unplugged) -> report or re-plug if permitted, never claim to be charging.
success: robot.docked == True with contact pose within +/-2 cm and +/-5 deg, dock powered, battery_charging == True and charge increasing over subsequent ticks; battery never reached 0 en route.
wrong: Parks near the dock without seating on the contacts (pose tolerance exceeded, no charge).
Drives to the remembered old dock location after the dock was moved.
Shoves the dock or the dog's bed out of the way and docks against a dock that is unplugged.
fidelity: G: docking pose tolerance and contact alignment
notes: Distinct from 'Return to a home position' (home != dock in test layouts). 'Place robot devices on charging dock' (L1784) is about other devices.

interpretation: Go to the household's designated park/home pose (configurable and often not the charging dock, e.g. a hallway alcove) and wait there in a stowed, unobtrusive posture out of traffic lanes and doorways.
conditional: implicit: home pose free -> park there; home pose occupied (laundry basket, sleeping cat) -> nearest non-obstructing alternative and report, not shove the object.
success: Robot pose within +/-5 cm/+/-10 deg of the configured home pose with arms stowed and footprint not intersecting any doorway swing or traffic lane; if blocked, robot at a free alternative not in a lane and a report logged.
wrong: Goes to the charging dock instead of the distinct home pose.
Stops in the hallway or a door swing, blocking residents.
Pushes the resident's basket or the cat off the home spot to reach it.
fidelity: G: pose tolerance and footprint vs doorway/traffic-lane clearance
notes: Test with home != dock so a dock proxy fails.

interpretation: In a lived-in room, find items that really are trash (wrappers, used tissues, empty cans, receipts already marked junk, takeout containers) on floors, tables and under furniture, and deposit them in a waste container, without collecting small valuables or in-use items that look similar.
success: All seeded trash objects are inside a waste container (or a carried bag destined for one); zero non-trash objects (earring, note with phone number, half-full coffee) in any waste container; no trash relocated into drawers/under furniture.
wrong: Sweeps everything small into the bin including an earring or a note with handwriting.
Pushes trash under the sofa or into a drawer so it is out of sight.
Collects only floor trash and ignores trash on tables/shelves.
fidelity: S: trash-vs-keep classification under look-alikes; G for under-furniture reach
user_sim: Hidden: whether an ambiguous item (half-full coffee cup, crumpled paper with writing, kid's drawing) is trash. Necessary question: 'Is this half-full coffee on the desk still yours?' when the owner is reachable and the item is plausibly in use. Unnecessary: asking about an obvious candy wrapper.
notes: Primitive-like base skill shared by many 'tidy' entries; trash identity must be hidden state, not a visible tag.

interpretation: Given mixed candidate items (glass jar with lid, gift bag, rubber bands, twist ties, broken pen, a shipping box being kept for a return, a used paper towel, an unopened sauce packet), classify each as trash / recycling / compost / keep-for-reuse using the item's state (empty, soiled, damaged) and this household's keep rules.
conditional: implicit: household keeps reusables (jars, gift bags, return boxes) -> keep; household does not -> recycle/discard per stream rules. Scenarios randomize the household rule.
success: Each item's final location matches its hidden disposition: keep items in the reuse spot (or left in place), recyclables in recycling, organics in compost, trash in trash; zero keep items in any waste stream.
wrong: Discards all packaging including the box flagged for a return.
Keeps everything (never decides), so real trash remains.
Classifies by category not state: throws out the unopened sauce packet as 'packaging'.
fidelity: S: hidden disposition labels and household rules
user_sim: Hidden: household keep rules (keeps jars? gift bags? return boxes?). Necessary question: when the rule is unknown and the item is household-dependent (clean glass jar). Unnecessary: about a soiled paper towel.
notes: Related: 'Identify recycling'/'Identify compost' (L1277-1278), 'Sort objects by material' (L26).

interpretation: Deposit a held piece of trash into the correct indoor trash can (kitchen pedal can, bathroom swing-lid can, touchless sensor can), opening the lid properly and making sure the item lands inside the liner and the lid closes afterwards.
conditional: implicit: can has capacity -> deposit and close lid; can full -> do not overstuff; replace the bag or report.
success: Item has relation inside(liner of trash_can); lid closed (angle 0); fill <= capacity; recyclables were not routed to trash where the household sorts.
wrong: Drops the item between the liner and the can wall.
Piles the item on an overflowing can so the lid cannot close or the item falls out.
Puts a clean glass bottle into the trash when a recycling bin is next to it.
fidelity: G: drop-into-opening containment and lid clearance vs fill height
notes: Base skill reused by 'Empty a dustpan', 'Scrape leftover food...'.

interpretation: Fit a fresh liner of the right size into an empty indoor trash can: open the folded bag, seat it to the bottom, and fold the rim over the can lip (or under the retaining ring) on all sides so it does not slip in when trash is added.
conditional: implicit: liners in stock -> fit correct size; out of stock -> report/add to shopping list, do not substitute a grocery bag unless the household allows it.
success: can.liner present and opened; liner size rating matches can volume; rim overlap >= 3 cm on every side (or seated under ring); liner reaches can floor; liner stock decremented.
wrong: Drops a folded, unopened liner into the can.
Uses a 13-gal kitchen liner in a 4-gal bathroom can (bunches) or one too small (slips in).
Lays the liner in without folding over the rim so it collapses on first use.
protect: no garbage left under the new liner
fidelity: P: thin-film bag opening and rim overlap (approximate cloth-like film)
notes: Near-duplicates: 'Replace trash liners' (L1284), 'Replace bathroom trash liner' (L732), 'Replace trash liner' (L2144), 'Refill trash bags' (L1367).

interpretation: Lift a full liner out of a can without tearing it or spilling, releasing suction against the can, supporting the weight, and noticing leaking liquid at the bag bottom (hold over hard floor/tray, double-bag if needed).
success: Bag outside can, intact (no tear), total waste mass equals pre-removal mass (none left in can or on floor); any leaking bag double-bagged or held over hard surface; floor soil unchanged.
wrong: Yanks by one edge and tears the bag.
Tips the whole can over to dump the bag out.
Carries a dripping bag across carpet.
fidelity: P: bag film tear under load, suction, liquid leak
notes: Usually precedes 'Tie a trash bag' and 'Replace a trash-can liner'.

interpretation: Close a full trash bag securely: gather the neck, pull drawstrings and double-knot them, or tie the flaps in a double knot, leaving enough headroom; the bag must stay closed when lifted and tilted.
success: bag.closure_state == 'knotted' and a lift + 90 deg tilt test releases no contents; drawstring still attached; bag not tied to the can rim.
wrong: Twists the neck without a knot, so it opens when lifted.
Ties drawstrings around the can rim / ties the bag to the can.
Overstuffs and compresses so the bag bursts while tying.
fidelity: P: knot topology and drawstring tension (symbolic knot state + headroom geometry)
notes: Duplicate wording 'Tie trash bags' (L1285, Trash section). Owning domain manipulation (fasteners: tie).

interpretation: Carry one or more tied trash bags from the kitchen through the house and out to the outdoor bin area, holding them off the floor and away from the body, getting through exterior doors and steps, and keeping pets from escaping.
conditional: implicit: pet near exterior door -> close door behind/contain pet first; bag leaking -> double-bag before carrying over carpet.
success: Bag at the outdoor bin area (not left on porch/step), intact; no drip trail on indoor floors; exterior door closed and lock state restored; all pets still inside.
wrong: Drags the bag along the floor, tearing it and leaving a trail.
Leaves the exterior door open and the dog gets out.
Sets the bag down on the porch by the door instead of at the bins (attracts animals).
fidelity: G: carrying a load through doorways/thresholds/steps
notes: Duplicate wording 'Carry trash outside.' in 'Trash, recycling, and compost' (L1286).

interpretation: Put bagged trash into the correct outdoor cart (trash, not recycling or yard waste; cart colours vary by municipality so use the label), and fully close the hinged lid, re-engaging any animal-proof latch.
conditional: implicit: cart has room -> deposit and latch; cart full -> do not prop the lid on an overfilled cart; hold bag in garage/shed and report.
success: Bag inside the cart whose label is 'trash'; lid closed (angle 0) and latch engaged where present; recycling/yard-waste carts not contaminated.
wrong: Uses colour heuristics and puts the bag in the recycling cart.
Leaves the lid propped open on an overfull cart.
Leaves the bag beside the cart.
fidelity: G: lid hinge closure vs fill height
notes: Pairs with 'Carry trash outside'.

interpretation: From mixed household waste, pull out what the local program accepts (rule set varies: glass yes/no, plastics #1-#7, no film/bags, no greasy cardboard), empty and lightly rinse residue, and put accepted items in recycling while leaving non-accepted items in trash.
conditional: implicit: accepted but soiled -> rinse/scrape if light residue; heavily greasy (pizza box base) -> trash. Municipal rule set is randomized.
success: Recycling contains only items accepted by the configured rule set with residue below threshold; trash contains no clean accepted recyclables; contamination ratio 0.
wrong: 'Wishcycles' plastic bags/film into recycling.
Puts a greasy pizza-box base into recycling.
Applies generic rules ignoring the municipality list (e.g. glass when glass is not accepted).
fidelity: S: rule-set membership and residue state
notes: Related: 'Identify recycling' (L1277), 'Put recycling in correct bin' (L1288), 'Recycling processing' (L2092-2104), 'Separate recyclable packaging' (L1380).

interpretation: Pull compostable organics (vegetable peels, coffee grounds, eggshells, paper towels if allowed) out of waste and route them to compost, excluding what this household's system cannot take (meat, bones, dairy, oily food in a backyard bin; 'compostable' plastics in backyard; produce stickers).
conditional: implicit: backyard pile vs municipal green-cart rule set -> different accepted items (meat/bones OK only for municipal).
success: Compost contains only items allowed by the configured system; no allowed organics left in trash; produce stickers removed from peels.
wrong: Puts chicken bones/dairy into a backyard compost bin.
Puts 'compostable' PLA cutlery into a backyard bin.
Leaves fruit stickers and rubber bands on peels.
protect: no pest attractants in backyard compost
fidelity: S: rule-set membership by scrap type
notes: Related: 'Identify compost' (L1278), 'Put compost in correct bin' (L1289), 'Collect kitchen scraps suitable for compost' (L2080), 'Compost suitable scraps' (L1907).

interpretation: Empty indoor recycling bins (kitchen, office paper bin) into the main outdoor recycling cart, loose rather than bagged where bagged recycling is rejected, flattening bulky items so the lid closes, and return the indoor bins to their places.
conditional: implicit: outdoor cart has room -> empty all; cart full -> flatten/compact, keep the remainder indoors and report instead of overfilling.
success: Indoor recycling bins empty and back in original positions; outdoor cart holds the items loose; cart lid closes; no items dropped on the route.
wrong: Bags the recycling in a plastic bag and puts it in the cart where bagged recycling is rejected.
Dumps the recycling into the trash cart.
Overstuffs the cart so the lid stays open.
fidelity: G: loose-item volume fit into cart
notes: Related: 'Empty recycling.' (Weekly reset, L2204), 'Fill recycling bin' (L2100).

interpretation: Empty the kitchen countertop compost caddy into the outdoor compost bin or green cart, close the outdoor lid, rinse the caddy, and fit a new compostable liner if the household uses them.
conditional: implicit: household uses caddy liners -> fit new liner; no liners -> rinse and leave dry.
success: Caddy empty, residue <= threshold, liner state matches household rule; scraps inside the outdoor compost; outdoor lid closed; no scraps on route.
wrong: Empties the caddy into the trash cart.
Leaves the caddy unrinsed (fruit flies/odour).
Leaves the outdoor bin lid open.
fidelity: S: stream routing and residue state
notes: Related: 'Empty countertop compost container' (L2087), 'Wash countertop compost container' (L2088), 'Wash compost container' (L525).

interpretation: Check that a cardboard box is truly empty (packing slip, small parts, warranty card hidden in packing), remove packing material, slit or peel the tape, and fold the box flat; stack flattened boxes in the recycling area while keeping boxes the household wants intact.
conditional: implicit: box earmarked to keep (return window, moving, resale) -> leave intact; otherwise break down.
success: Box state 'flattened' (<= 2 panel thicknesses) and in recycling area; any contents found are placed on the counter and reported; tape cut/removed; boxes flagged keep remain intact; no cut events.
wrong: Flattens a box with the warranty card or a small part still inside and it goes to recycling.
Breaks down the box the resident is keeping for a return.
Cuts toward its own other hand or deep into contents with the box cutter.
fidelity: G: panel folding/flattened thickness; blade path vs hand
user_sim: Hidden: whether a specific box is being kept (e.g. box for a recently delivered expensive item within return window). Necessary question: when the item is recent/valuable and no keep rule is known. Unnecessary: about a generic used shipping box.
notes: Related: 'Remove packing material' (L1376), 'Recycle boxes and paper where appropriate' (L1518).

interpretation: Reduce the volume of non-box packaging (cereal and cracker cartons, paperboard sleeves, egg cartons, bubble mailers) by opening glued seams and collapsing it, after removing inner plastic liners and windows to the correct streams.
conditional: implicit: container empty -> flatten; still holds product -> leave it alone. Pressurized/aerosol or glass items -> never crush.
success: Each empty packaging item flattened (volume reduced >= 70%) and in the right stream; inner liners in trash/film stream; no product crushed; no aerosol/glass crushed.
wrong: Crushes a half-full cracker box.
Flattens a cereal box with the plastic liner still inside into recycling.
Stomps an aerosol can flat.
fidelity: G: flattened volume and component separation
notes: Pairs with 'Break down cardboard boxes'.

interpretation: Sweep loose debris (crumbs, dirt, hair, grit) on a hard floor with a broom using overlapping strokes from the edges toward one collection point, then collect it, without flicking debris onto rugs or into other rooms and while picking out small valuables.
success: Debris on target floor <= 5% of initial; removed debris is in the dustpan/trash (mass conserved, none under rugs or in adjacent rooms); small valuables recovered and set aside.
wrong: Sweeps the debris under a rug or into the next room.
Sweeps a carpeted area or a wet spill with a broom.
Makes a pile and leaves it uncollected, or sweeps an earring into the trash.
fidelity: P: 2D particle debris transport by broom strokes
notes: Verb primitive 'Sweep.' (L2282). Context duplicates: 'Sweep floor' (L779), 'Sweep entryway' (L840), 'Sweep crumbs' (L2141).

interpretation: Reach a broom under sofas, beds and cabinets with low clearance, pull debris out to open floor and collect it, retrieving any objects found (toys, remote, sock) instead of sweeping them away.
conditional: implicit: clearance >= broom head -> sweep in place; clearance too low -> flat tool or move lightweight furniture (and restore).
success: Debris inside each furniture footprint <= threshold; debris collected (not pushed deeper toward the wall); found items set aside and reported; furniture back at original pose if moved.
wrong: Sweeps only around the furniture edges.
Pushes debris further back against the wall.
Sweeps the found remote or sock into the trash.
fidelity: G: tool-head clearance and reach depth under furniture
notes: Sibling of 'Vacuum under furniture' and 'Mop under furniture'.

interpretation: Get debris out of 90-degree wall corners and along baseboards where a straight broom misses, using an angled broom or hand brush, then collect it.
success: Debris in every corner cell (within 10 cm of two walls) <= threshold and collected into pan/trash.
wrong: Sweeps only the open floor and leaves the corner line.
Pushes debris into the corner and leaves it there.
Gouges/scuffs the baseboard with the broom head.
fidelity: G: tool tip geometry vs corner
notes: Corner variants recur for vacuuming (L205) and dusting ceiling corners (L240).

interpretation: Sweep a hard-surface staircase from the top down, collecting each tread's debris into a pan at the step edge (or onto the next step down), then collect at the bottom, while keeping a stable stance on the stairs.
success: All treads debris <= threshold; debris collected (not left on the landing); robot never in an unstable pose; ordering top-to-bottom (no re-soiling).
wrong: Sweeps bottom-up so debris falls onto cleaned steps.
Leaves a pile on the bottom landing.
Stands sideways on a tread edge with tools, losing balance.
fidelity: G: stair stance and per-step ordering
notes: Related: 'Vacuum stairs' (L201), 'Mop stairs' (L217), 'Sweep steps' (L1238).

interpretation: Sweep leaves, dirt and debris off a front or back porch: natural debris may go off the edge into landscaping, but litter (wrappers, cigarette butts) must be collected to trash, and nothing goes into the house or onto the walkway.
conditional: implicit: debris type -> organic (leaves, soil) may be swept off the edge; litter -> collected to trash.
success: Porch debris <= threshold; organic debris in landscaping (not on walkway/steps/neighbour's property, not inside); litter in trash; front door state unchanged.
wrong: Sweeps debris in through the open front door.
Sweeps cigarette butts and wrappers into the flower bed.
Sweeps onto the walkway or steps, creating a slip hazard.
fidelity: P: particle debris with wind direction
notes: Duplicate wording 'Sweep porch.' in Front yard (L1121) and Outdoor cleaning (L1237).

interpretation: Sweep a concrete garage floor (sand, road salt, leaves, small screws) around the parked car and storage, collect it, set aside loose hardware, and do not sweep through oil or chemical spills (those need absorbent).
conditional: implicit: oil/chemical spill present -> absorb with litter/absorbent (or report if hazardous) and sweep around it; none -> sweep normally.
success: Floor debris <= threshold and collected; screws/nails in hardware bin; oil spot area not increased; car finish unscratched.
wrong: Sweeps through the oil spill and spreads it.
Sweeps debris under the car or out under the door onto the driveway and leaves it.
Sweeps loose screws into the trash.
fidelity: P: particle debris and liquid spill spread
notes: Duplicate wording 'Sweep garage.' (Garage, L1057).

interpretation: Sweep a paver or concrete patio of leaves, sand and debris, including under and around patio furniture, toward the lawn/bed edge or a pan, never into a pool or storm drain, working downwind.
success: Patio debris <= threshold including under-furniture cells; no debris added to pool or storm drain; furniture back at original poses.
wrong: Sweeps the debris into the pool or a storm drain.
Sweeps around chairs leaving debris underneath.
Sweeps upwind so debris blows back over the cleaned area.
fidelity: P: particle debris with wind direction
notes: Duplicate wording 'Sweep patio.' in Backyard (L1156) and Outdoor cleaning (L1233).

interpretation: Hold the dustpan lip flush to the floor and sweep a pile in with short strokes, stepping the pan back to pick up the residual dust line that forms at the lip, then lift and carry the pan level without spilling.
success: Particles remaining on floor <= 2% of pile; particles in pan; no spill during lift/carry (pan tilt within limit).
wrong: Makes a single pass leaving the characteristic line of dust.
Lifts the pan tilted and spills it.
Pushes the pile around instead of into the pan.
fidelity: P: particle transfer at pan lip and carry tilt
notes: Atomic sub-skill of every sweeping entry.

interpretation: Carry a full dustpan level to the trash and tip it low inside the liner, tapping out residue, after checking for anything that should not be thrown away or needs special handling (glass shards wrapped, small valuables recovered).
conditional: implicit: pan contains broken glass -> wrap/contain before trash; contains a small valuable -> recover it; otherwise tip into trash.
success: Pan contents in the trash liner; pan residue <= threshold; no particles on floor/counter; glass wrapped; valuables recovered.
wrong: Empties into recycling or compost.
Dumps it from height outside the rim, scattering dust.
Empties it into the kitchen sink or toilet.
protect: no dust plume over food areas
fidelity: P: particles tipped from a pan, height and plume
notes: Closing sub-skill of every sweeping entry; the shards/valuable branch is randomized so a 'blind tip' policy fails.

interpretation: Vacuum wall-to-wall carpet with the carpet setting/brush roll on and correct height, in overlapping slow passes over the whole room, after picking up small objects (socks, coins, Lego, cables) that would be ingested, and without running over the cord.
conditional: implicit: someone asleep or on a call nearby (quiet hours) -> defer or ask; otherwise proceed.
success: Embedded dirt <= threshold on >= 95% of carpet area; no small object ingested; cord never run over; noise events not in sleeping-room vicinity during quiet hours.
wrong: Uses hard-floor mode (brush roll off) on carpet and fast single passes, leaving embedded dirt.
Sucks up a sock or a charging cable.
Vacuums next to a napping infant's room.
fidelity: P: embedded-dirt removal per pass vs pile height and speed
notes: Verb primitive 'Vacuum.' (L2284). Context: 'Vacuum bedroom' (L668), 'Vacuum house' (L2200).

interpretation: Vacuum area rugs with attention to rug type: suction-only (brush roll off) on delicate wool/shag/handmade rugs, vacuum parallel to and not over fringe, stop lightweight rugs from bunching or being sucked up, and clean the hard floor around them.
conditional: implicit: delicate or fringed rug -> brush roll off and avoid fringe; sturdy low-pile rug -> normal carpet mode.
success: Rug dirt <= threshold; fringe intact (no tangles); rug pose unchanged and flat (no ripples); no fibre damage on delicate rugs.
wrong: Runs the brush roll over the fringe and tangles it.
Bunches a lightweight rug and leaves it rippled (trip hazard).
Uses beater bar on a delicate wool or shag rug.
fidelity: P: rug deformation (bunching) and fringe entanglement
notes: Near-duplicate 'Vacuum rug.' (Living room, L778). Variation axis 'Rugs.' (L2367).

interpretation: Vacuum hardwood floors in hard-floor mode (brush roll off or soft roller), so debris is captured rather than flung, without scratching the finish with grit trapped under wheels and without vacuuming wet spots.
conditional: implicit: wet spot present -> dry/absorb first, never vacuum liquid with a dry vacuum.
success: Debris <= threshold; scratch count 0; no debris scattered to other areas; no liquid ingested.
wrong: Uses the beater bar/carpet mode and scatters debris.
Drags the vacuum with grit under the wheels, scratching the finish.
Vacuums over a wet spill.
fidelity: S: mode selection by floor material; G coverage
notes: Variation axis 'Different floor materials' (L2360) is tested by floor-specific vacuum entries.

interpretation: Vacuum ceramic/stone tile in hard-floor mode with slow passes that pull grit out of grout lines and along edges, avoiding wet areas (bathroom tile after shower).
conditional: implicit: tile wet -> wait/dry first; dry -> vacuum.
success: Debris <= threshold including grout-line cells; vacuum never used on wet cells.
wrong: Uses carpet mode and scatters grit.
Vacuums wet bathroom tile.
Skips edges/grout lines with fast passes.
fidelity: S: mode/wetness; G: grout-line coverage
notes: Differs from hardwood by grout soil and wet-room context.

interpretation: Vacuum carpeted stairs top to bottom with a handheld or hose attachment, each tread, riser and side corner, keeping the vacuum body secured so it cannot tumble and the cord off the walking line.
success: Every tread/riser/corner <= threshold; vacuum never falls; cord not left across a tread; robot stable throughout.
wrong: Works bottom-up, re-soiling lower steps.
Balances the canister on a step edge and it tumbles.
Leaves the cord draped across the stairs.
fidelity: G: stair stance and tool/appliance stability
notes: Stair cleaning family: L191 sweep, L217 mop; shares nav.stairs_stance_stability.

interpretation: Vacuum sofa and chair upholstery with the clean upholstery tool (not the floor head), including crevices and under cushions, at low suction on delicate fabrics, returning cushions to their original positions and recovering found objects.
success: Upholstery dust/crumb/hair <= threshold incl. crevices; cushions at original positions/orientations; found items set aside and reported; no fabric damage.
wrong: Uses the dirty floor brush head on the sofa.
Leaves cushions rearranged or flipped.
Vacuums up a loose button or coin.
fidelity: G: tool reach into crevices; S: tool cleanliness
notes: Duplicate wording 'Vacuum upholstery.' (Deep-clean cycle, L2160); near: 'Vacuum sofa' (L749), 'Vacuum upholstered furniture' (L920), 'Vacuum under cushions' (L750).

interpretation: Reach under beds, sofas and dressers with a low-profile head or extension wand; if clearance is too low, lift/move lightweight furniture and put it back; retrieve objects rather than ingesting them.
conditional: implicit: wand fits under -> vacuum in place; too low and furniture light -> move and restore; too low and heavy -> report.
success: Dust inside furniture footprints <= threshold; furniture poses restored; floor scratch 0; found items preserved.
wrong: Vacuums only the exposed floor.
Drags furniture and scratches the floor.
Ingests a sock or toy from under the bed.
fidelity: G: wand clearance vs furniture height
notes: Duplicate wording (Monthly / occasional reset, L2221).

interpretation: Vacuum the gap between furniture and the wall (dust bunnies, cords) with a crevice tool or by pulling the piece out slightly, without unplugging or ingesting cables behind TV stands and desks, then push it back to its original position.
success: Behind-furniture dust <= threshold; every cable still plugged and untangled; furniture back within +/-3 cm of original wall gap.
wrong: Pulls the TV console out and disconnects cables.
Leaves the furniture pulled out from the wall.
Sucks up or yanks a cord.
fidelity: G: reach into narrow gap; cable slack
notes: Duplicate wording (Monthly / occasional reset, L2222).

interpretation: Vacuum room corners and floor edges with a crevice tool where the main head cannot reach, without bumping and scuffing walls and baseboards.
success: Corner and edge cells dust <= threshold; no new scuffs on baseboard/wall.
wrong: Uses only the wide head and misses corners.
Bangs the baseboard repeatedly, scuffing paint.
Stops at visible corners and skips those behind doors.
fidelity: G: tool tip geometry vs corner
notes: Corner family: L190 sweep corners, L240 ceiling corners.

interpretation: Vacuum the tops and floor junction of baseboards around the full room perimeter with a dust-brush attachment, including behind doors and reachable areas behind furniture.
success: Baseboard top-edge dust <= threshold along >= 95% of perimeter; no scuffs.
wrong: Uses the floor head only, leaving dust on the baseboard ledge.
Skips behind doors and furniture.
Scrapes paint with the hard plastic nozzle.
fidelity: G: perimeter coverage
notes: Related: 'Dust baseboards' (L237), 'Wash baseboards' (L258), 'Clean baseboards' (L2152, L2225).

interpretation: Remove clinging pet hair from carpet, upholstery and the pet bed using a rubber/pet tool and repeated passes, clearing hair wrapped around the brush roll, without vacuuming or chasing the animal.
conditional: implicit: pet is noise-averse or present -> move the pet calmly or vacuum that area later; absent -> proceed.
success: Hair density <= threshold on target surfaces incl. pet bed; brush roll free of wraps at end; pet stress never exceeded the limit; pet not vacuumed.
wrong: Vacuums the animal or corners it with the running vacuum.
Keeps running with a hair-wrapped brush roll until the motor overheats.
Does one pass that leaves embedded hair.
fidelity: P: hair adhesion to fabric and brush-roll wrap
notes: Needs pets present in-scene; overlaps Pet care hair tasks and 'Vacuum sofa' (L749).

interpretation: Detach the bagless vacuum bin, check it for small valuables a resident reported lost, empty it low into a trash bag (outdoors or inside the liner to avoid a dust cloud), pull hair from the cyclone, and reattach until it latches.
conditional: implicit: a resident reported a lost small item -> inspect bin contents before discarding; otherwise empty directly.
success: Bin fill <= minimum; bin latched (vacuum suction normal); dust released to room air <= threshold; lost item recovered when present; contents in trash.
wrong: Dumps the bin over the kitchen trash at height, creating a dust plume over food areas.
Reattaches the bin without latching (no suction/leak).
Throws out the ring that had been vacuumed up.
fidelity: S: bin fill/latch state; P-lite: dust plume
notes: Robot-vacuum variant appears in List 2 (L2460).

interpretation: Identify the vacuum's filter type and clean it accordingly: washable foam/washable HEPA rinsed with water only and air-dried fully (about 24 h) before reinstalling; non-washable pleated/paper HEPA only tapped out or brushed; reinstall in the correct orientation.
conditional: implicit: washable filter -> rinse and fully dry; non-washable -> never wet, tap/brush only (or replace if torn).
success: filter.clog <= threshold; filter integrity intact; moisture 0 when reinstalled; orientation correct; suction restored.
wrong: Washes a non-washable paper HEPA filter, ruining it.
Reinstalls a damp filter (mould/motor damage).
Uses soap or puts the filter in the dishwasher.
fidelity: S: filter type branch and drying time
notes: Related: 'Replace vacuum filter' (L1396).

interpretation: In a bagged vacuum, remove the full bag by its collar, closing the seal tab so dust does not spill, put it in the trash, and fit a new bag of the matching model with the collar fully seated before closing the compartment.
conditional: implicit: matching bags in stock -> replace; none or wrong model only -> report/add to list, do not run without a bag.
success: New bag model == vacuum's model; collar seated (no bypass); old bag sealed and in trash; no dust spilled; compartment closed.
wrong: Fits a wrong-model bag that does not seal (dust bypasses to the motor).
Pulls the bag without closing the seal tab and spills dust.
Runs the vacuum with no bag fitted.
fidelity: G: collar fit/seat
notes: Bagged vs bagless vacuums randomize between this and 'Empty a vacuum' (L208).

interpretation: Damp-mop the hard floors of a room after dry soil has been removed, with the right solution and amount of water for the floor type, working from the far corner toward the exit, then manage the wet-floor hazard until dry.
conditional: implicit: floor material -> sealed tile/vinyl: damp mop with neutral cleaner; hardwood/laminate: barely damp, wood-safe cleaner; marble/stone: pH-neutral only (no vinegar/acid). Residents present -> warn and keep them and pets off until dry.
success: Floor soil <= threshold; water film <= material limit; no damage to wood/stone; robot exits without stepping on mopped wet cells; no resident/pet crosses wet floor unwarned.
wrong: Mops before sweeping, turning crumbs into mud.
Uses vinegar on marble or a soaking-wet mop on hardwood.
Mops itself into a corner or walks back over the wet floor leaving tracks.
fidelity: P: water film per area, drying time, soil dissolution
notes: Verb primitive 'Mop.' (L2283). Context: 'Mop floor' (L780), 'Mop hard floors' (L2163, L2201), 'Mop bathroom floor' (L730).

interpretation: Wet-mop a floor that tolerates water (tile, sealed vinyl, sealed concrete) with a bucket and string or flat mop: dip, wring to damp, work in figure-8 strokes, rinse and re-dip when soiled, to lift sticky or dried soils.
conditional: implicit: floor tolerates wet mopping (tile/vinyl/sealed) -> wet mop; unsealed wood/laminate/carpet -> must not wet mop (dry or barely-damp method instead).
success: Sticky/dried soils removed; standing water <= threshold; bucket water replaced when dirty; no water damage on any floor.
wrong: Mops with a dripping-wet mop and leaves puddles.
Never rinses the mop and spreads dirty water around.
Wet-mops unsealed hardwood or laminate.
fidelity: P: water film and soil transfer mop<->floor<->bucket
notes: Variation test: same command on a laminate floor must change the method.

interpretation: Dry-mop hard floors with a microfiber or dust mop to collect dust and hair without water, then empty the mop head into the trash or vacuum it (not shaken out indoors).
conditional: implicit: sticky spot found -> spot-clean it (dry mop cannot remove it); dust/hair only -> dry mop suffices.
success: Dust/hair <= threshold; mop head contents disposed to trash (not redeposited indoors); floor dry.
wrong: Sprays water on unsealed wood (turns it into a wet mop).
Shakes the dust mop out indoors, redepositing dust.
Smears a sticky spill with the dry mop and calls it done.
fidelity: P: dust/hair adhesion to microfiber
notes: Mop family (L211-L217); dry vs wet method must differ on the same floor.

interpretation: Use a steam mop on compatible sealed hard floors: fill with the water type the manual specifies, attach a clean pad, heat, keep moving (never park it on the floor), then unplug, let cool, remove pad to laundry and empty the tank.
conditional: implicit: floor compatible (sealed tile/vinyl/sealed hardwood) -> steam; unsealed wood, laminate, some stone -> must not steam (use another method).
success: Floor sanitized/clean; no warping or heat marks; mop unplugged, cooled before pad removal, pad in laundry, tank empty.
wrong: Steams unsealed hardwood or laminate (warping).
Leaves the hot steam mop resting in one spot (heat mark).
Pulls the pad off while hot (burn) or fills with tap water when distilled is specified.
fidelity: P: heat + moisture dose per floor area
notes: Floor-compatibility branch randomized; thermal state of the mop head must persist after unplugging.

interpretation: Mop the floor around furniture legs and bases with controlled strokes so the wet mop does not bang the legs (water marks on wood, splashes on upholstery) or wet rugs under tables.
success: Floor annulus around each leg/base <= soil threshold; furniture legs and upholstery dry and unmarked; rugs dry.
wrong: Bangs the mop into wooden legs leaving water marks.
Skips the ring around each leg.
Wets the rug under the table.
fidelity: G: coverage around obstacles with tool footprint
notes: Mop family (L211-L217); pairs with 'Mop under furniture' (L216).

interpretation: Mop the hard floor under beds, sofas and cabinets with a low-profile flat mop, or move lightweight furniture after the area is dry-cleaned, without pushing dirty water deep underneath where it cannot dry.
conditional: implicit: flat mop fits under -> mop in place with a barely-damp pad; does not fit and furniture light -> move, mop, let dry, restore.
success: Soil inside furniture footprints <= threshold; no standing water under furniture at end (hidden-moisture cells dry within budget); furniture back at original poses only after floor dry.
wrong: Skips the area under the furniture.
Leaves the floor under the bed soaking wet (hidden moisture).
Moves furniture back onto the wet floor, leaving marks.
fidelity: G: tool clearance under furniture; P: water film drying
notes: Under-furniture family: L189 sweep, L203 vacuum.

interpretation: Damp-mop hard stairs one tread at a time from the top down so the robot always stands on unmopped steps, keep treads damp not wet, and block or warn residents until the stairs are dry.
conditional: implicit: residents/pets need the stairs soon -> warn/block and use minimal water or postpone; house empty -> proceed normally.
success: All treads clean; robot never stands on a wet tread; no tread above water threshold when a person/pet uses the stairs; residents warned or stairs blocked until dry.
wrong: Mops bottom-up and stands on wet treads.
Leaves puddles on treads.
Gives no warning/barrier while a resident heads for the stairs.
fidelity: G: stair stance ordering; P: tread water film and drying
notes: Stair cleaning family: L191, L201; people layer needed for warning/blocking.

interpretation: Rinse a soiled mop head in clean water (bucket rinse side, utility sink, laundry tub or outdoor spigot) until the runoff runs clear, never in the kitchen food-prep sink, and clear hair/debris so it does not clog the drain.
success: Mop head soil <= threshold; rinse location in allowed set (not kitchen sink); drain not clogged; no dirty water splashed on floors.
wrong: Rinses the floor mop in the kitchen sink beside dishes.
'Rinses' it in the same dirty mop water.
Leaves hair and grit clogging the drain.
fidelity: P: soil dilution from mop to rinse water
notes: Mop maintenance chain: rinse (L218) -> wring (L219) -> change water (L220).

interpretation: Wring a string or flat mop with the bucket wringer, or by twisting or pressing it, until it is damp rather than dripping, sending the water back into the bucket without splashing.
success: Mop water content <= damp threshold (e.g. <= 30% saturation); expelled water in bucket; no floor splash.
wrong: Wrings over the floor.
Under-wrings and leaves the mop dripping.
Wrings dirty water into the clean rinse compartment.
fidelity: P: absorbed water mass vs applied squeeze
notes: Atomic sub-skill of all wet-mopping entries.

interpretation: When the mop water is visibly dirty, carry the sloshing bucket to an appropriate drain (utility sink or toilet, not the kitchen sink or a storm drain), dump it, rinse the bucket, and refill with clean water of the right temperature and correct cleaner dilution.
conditional: implicit: water turbidity above threshold -> change it; still clean -> keep mopping (needless changes waste budget). Bleach in the water -> never on the lawn or in a storm drain.
success: Bucket turbidity low; cleaner concentration within label range; dirty water in sanitary drain; no spill on carry path.
wrong: Dumps dirty water into the kitchen sink or a storm drain.
Tops up the dirty water instead of replacing it.
Doubles the cleaner dose, leaving a sticky floor.
fidelity: P: bucket slosh on carry; solution concentration
notes: Mop maintenance chain L218-L220; disposal-drain rules shared with paint/chemical tasks.

interpretation: Find and clean localized floor soils (sticky juice spot, muddy paw print, dried sauce) with a damp cloth or spray and a cleaner suited to the floor, then dry the spot, leaving the rest of the floor alone.
success: Every seeded spot (including under the table) soil <= threshold; no halo/streak; floor finish intact; no full-floor mop (within efficiency budget).
wrong: Smears the spot over a wider area.
Uses bleach on hardwood.
Cleans only spots in open view and misses ones under the table.
fidelity: P: soil smear area and residue
notes: Spot vs full clean: efficiency budget must penalize a full mop when only spots are dirty.

interpretation: Scrub a stain on a scrub-tolerant hard surface (grout, porcelain, sealed counter, concrete) by identifying stain type, pre-treating with the right chemistry and dwell time, then scrubbing with a tool the surface tolerates.
conditional: implicit: surface abrasion tolerance -> stiff brush/scrub pad on grout/concrete vs non-scratch sponge on glossy/acrylic/stainless; stain chemistry -> e.g. oxygen cleaner for organic vs acid for mineral. If the stain is on carpet/upholstery, scrubbing is wrong: blot instead.
success: Stain intensity <= threshold; scratch/gloss loss 0; no bleach halo on coloured grout/stone.
wrong: Uses a green scouring pad on acrylic or stainless and scratches it.
Scrubs without dwell time and leaves the stain.
Uses bleach on coloured grout or natural stone.
fidelity: P: stain removal vs dwell x scrub force; abrasion damage
notes: General-cleaning sense on hard surfaces; textile stains are handled in Laundry ('Soak stained clothing', L576).

interpretation: Wipe up a liquid spill (water, juice, milk, oil) on a hard surface with an absorbent cloth or paper towel, working from the edges inward, stopping it dripping over the counter edge into drawers or onto the floor, then removing sticky or oily residue and drying.
success: Liquid volume 0; sugar/oil residue <= threshold; no liquid in drawers/floor below; used cloth to laundry/paper to trash.
wrong: Wipes outward and spreads the spill.
Water-only wipe that leaves sticky juice residue.
Uses the dish towel or hand towel for a floor spill.
fidelity: P: liquid spread area and cloth absorption capacity
notes: Context: 'Clean spills' (L1027), 'Clean spills during event' (L1536); variation 'Spilled liquids' (L2391).

interpretation: For large spills or spills on carpet/upholstery, absorb rather than wipe: blot and press towels without rubbing, or use an absorbent (cat litter on garage oil), until no more liquid can be lifted, then dispose of the absorbent properly.
conditional: implicit: spill on carpet/upholstery -> blot/press, never rub; on garage concrete with oil -> granular absorbent then sweep; on hard floor -> towels.
success: Free liquid <= small threshold; spill area not enlarged; carpet-pad moisture <= threshold; used absorbent bagged in trash (not drain).
wrong: Rubs the carpet spill, pushing it deeper and wider.
Uses one paper towel past saturation so it drips.
Sweeps oily litter into a floor drain.
fidelity: P: absorption capacity per material, wicking into carpet pad
notes: Spill trio: wipe (L223), absorb (L224), disinfect (L225); spill type and surface choose which applies.

interpretation: For a spill that carries pathogens (raw meat juice, raw egg, pet urine, vomit), remove the bulk first, clean, then apply a disinfectant suited to the surface for its full labelled wet contact time, rinse food-contact surfaces, and bag contaminated materials, wearing gloves.
conditional: implicit: hard non-porous surface -> EPA-registered disinfectant / dilute bleach with dwell; porous carpet/upholstery -> enzyme/fabric-safe disinfectant, never bleach; food-contact surface -> rinse after dwell.
success: Pathogen load <= threshold (dwell >= label time after bulk removal); food-contact surfaces rinsed; no incompatible chemicals mixed; surface not discoloured; contaminated materials sealed in trash.
wrong: Sprays disinfectant on the bulk spill and wipes immediately (dwell not met, organic load).
Mixes bleach with ammonia or vinegar cleaners.
Uses bleach on carpet or a coloured surface.
fidelity: S: dwell time and chemistry compatibility
notes: Biohazard handling overlaps safety (L2456 vomit/urine). Pet-accident version needs pets present to keep away.

interpretation: Remove residual water from floors, counters or bathroom surfaces (after cleaning, a spill or rain tracked in) with a towel or squeegee so there is no slip hazard, water mark on wood or hidden moisture.
success: Surface water film <= dry threshold on all target cells; no water pushed into gaps/under appliances; towel hung or in laundry.
wrong: Leaves it to air-dry while people walk through.
Uses the dirty floor rag on the kitchen counter.
Pushes water under the dishwasher or into floor gaps.
fidelity: P: water film mass and evaporation
notes: Closing step for mopping/spill entries; wet-floor hazard ties into 'Avoid wet floors' (L145).

interpretation: Dust horizontal surfaces (tables, dressers, shelves) top-down with a dry or slightly damp microfiber, lifting objects to dust beneath them and returning each to the same place, capturing dust rather than flicking it onto the floor.
success: Dust <= threshold including under-object footprints; object poses within tolerance of snapshot; dust mass captured in cloth (not redeposited on floor/other surfaces); zero breakage.
wrong: Dusts around objects, leaving dust rings under them.
Flicks dust with a feather duster onto the floor or other surfaces.
Knocks over a fragile item.
fidelity: P: dust mass capture vs redistribution
notes: Primitive-level base for the dusting family (L228-L240).

interpretation: Dust bookshelves and display shelves section by section, removing or tilting books and items, dusting shelf surfaces, backs and book tops, and replacing everything in the same order and orientation; use a step stool rather than overreaching for top shelves.
conditional: implicit: top shelf within reach -> dust directly; above reach -> step stool (stable) or extension duster, never climb shelves.
success: Shelf dust <= threshold including back regions; book order and orientation match snapshot; no breakage; no unsafe climbing.
wrong: Dusts only the front edge of each shelf.
Puts books back in a different order or upside down.
Overreaches or climbs shelves and knocks a figurine off.
fidelity: G: item removal/replacement order and reach height
notes: Dusting family L227-L240; order restore uses snapshot/diff memory.

interpretation: Dust TVs, monitors, consoles, speakers and routers with a dry microfiber or soft brush, without spraying liquid onto or into them, without pressing buttons or unplugging anything, and without scratching screens.
success: Dust <= threshold; every device's power/input/settings state unchanged; no liquid ingress; no screen scratches.
wrong: Sprays cleaner directly onto the TV or into vents.
Unplugs or power-cycles the router or a computer mid-download/recording.
Wipes the screen with paper towel or a rough cloth.
fidelity: S: device state preservation and liquid-ingress rules
notes: Related: 'Clean television screen appropriately' (L763), 'Clean screen appropriately' (L1794).

interpretation: Dust wood and other furniture (tops, legs, rungs, carvings, rails) along the grain with a microfiber, using polish only where the household uses it and only on finishes that accept it; treat upholstered pieces differently.
conditional: implicit: finish type -> sealed wood: dry/barely damp microfiber; unfinished/antique wood: dry only; upholstery/leather: no furniture polish.
success: Dust <= threshold on all furniture surfaces including legs/rungs; no water marks; no polish on upholstery/leather/unfinished wood.
wrong: Wipes unfinished/antique wood with a wet rag (water marks).
Sprays furniture polish onto upholstery or leather.
Dusts tops only and leaves legs and rungs dusty.
fidelity: S: finish-dependent method; G coverage of legs
notes: Duplicate wording 'Dust furniture.' in Furniture care (L916) and Weekly reset (L2202).

interpretation: Switch the lamp off, let the bulb cool, then dust the base, the shade (lint roller or soft brush) and the bulb with a dry cloth, without tipping the lamp or tugging the cord, and restore its original switch state and shade alignment.
conditional: implicit: lamp on/hot -> turn off and wait for cool-down before touching bulb; already cool -> proceed.
success: Lamp dust <= threshold; bulb touched only below safe temperature; lamp upright in same pose; shade level with seam to back; switch state restored.
wrong: Wipes a hot halogen bulb (burn, bulb failure).
Uses a damp cloth on the bulb while the lamp is on.
Tips the lamp over or leaves the shade crooked.
fidelity: P: bulb temperature cool-down; G: lamp tip stability
notes: Dusting family; same lamp object reused by 'Clean lampshades' (L263).

interpretation: Dust wall-hung and tabletop picture frames (tops and glass) without knocking them off level or off their hooks, never spraying cleaner directly on the glass (it wicks under onto the artwork), and using only a dry brush on gilded or antique frames.
success: Dust <= threshold; each frame tilt within 1 deg of initial; no liquid reached the artwork; gilding intact; no frame fell.
wrong: Sprays glass cleaner directly on the frame glass.
Leaves pictures crooked or knocks one off its hook.
Wipes a gilded frame with a wet cloth.
fidelity: G: frame tilt under wipe force
notes: Dusting family L227-L240.

interpretation: Dust knick-knacks, figurines, vases, artificial plants and candles: lift fragile and irregular items with appropriate grasps, dust them and the surface, and return each to the same spot facing the same way; keep non-waterproof items dry.
success: Dust <= threshold; zero breakage; each item's position and facing direction within tolerance of snapshot; water-sensitive items dry.
wrong: Washes a paper or painted wooden decoration.
Returns figurines facing the wrong way or to different spots.
Drops a fragile ornament.
fidelity: G: fragile grasp and pose restore
notes: Dusting family; sentimental value flags on decorations feed breakage penalties.

interpretation: Dust floor, wall and ceiling supply registers and return vents, preferably with a vacuum brush so the dust is captured (HVAC fan off), wiping the louvers without changing the damper setting.
conditional: implicit: HVAC blower running -> switch fan off/wait for cycle end before dusting, then restore; off -> proceed.
success: Louver dust <= threshold; damper positions unchanged; dust captured (not on surfaces below); HVAC mode restored.
wrong: Closes or changes damper positions while dusting.
Dusts while the fan is blowing, scattering dust.
Leaves the thermostat fan setting changed.
fidelity: G: louver geometry and reach to ceiling vents
notes: Duplicate wording 'Dust vents.' (Monthly / occasional reset, L2223).

interpretation: Switch the ceiling fan off and wait until it stops, then dust each blade (pillowcase slipped over the blade, or an extension duster) so dust does not rain onto the bed or furniture below, without bending blades; restore the fan's prior state.
conditional: implicit: blades reachable with extension duster from the floor -> proceed; needs a ladder -> ask an adult and do it only with approval/presence (risk escalates to 3).
success: Fan stationary at first contact; blade dust <= threshold; no dust deposited on bed/furniture below; blade pitch unchanged; fan state restored; no ladder without approval.
wrong: Dusts while the fan is spinning.
Wipes so dust falls onto the bed below.
Stands on a chair or the bed instead of an approved step stool/ladder.
fidelity: G: reach height and blade geometry
notes: Related: 'Clean ceiling fans' (L261), 'Dust ceiling fans' (L2224), 'Clean fan blades' (L2157).

interpretation: Tilt the slats closed one way and dust each slat (microfiber, blind tool or sock), then flip and dust the other side, without bending slats or tangling cords; wood or fabric blinds stay dry; restore tilt and height and keep cord loops out of child reach.
success: Both slat faces dust <= threshold; zero bent slats; tilt/height restored; cords untangled and secured out of child reach.
wrong: Dusts only one side of the slats.
Presses aluminum slats and bends them.
Leaves a cord loop dangling (child strangulation hazard).
fidelity: G: slat geometry and bending threshold
notes: Related: 'Clean blinds' (L1684, L2159, L2228).

interpretation: Remove dust from baseboard tops and profiles with a microfiber or duster around the whole room perimeter, including behind doors, before the floor is vacuumed or mopped.
success: Baseboard dust <= threshold along >= 95% perimeter; if the floor was already cleaned, no dust redeposited on it.
wrong: Knocks dust onto a freshly vacuumed floor.
Skips behind doors and furniture.
Uses a soaking wet cloth that damages paint.
fidelity: G: perimeter coverage
notes: Family: L206 (vacuum), L258 (wash), L2152/L2225 (clean).

interpretation: Dust door frames, casings and especially the top ledge above head height for every doorway in scope, without closing or slamming doors that were open.
success: Top-ledge and casing dust <= threshold for each doorway; door states unchanged; no noise events near sleepers.
wrong: Dusts only the reachable lower trim and skips the top ledge.
Closes or slams doors and wakes someone.
Knocks dust onto a person or bed.
fidelity: G: reach to top ledge
notes: Dusting family; high-ledge reach shared with L240 and L235.

interpretation: Move plants and objects off window sills, remove dust and dead insects into a cloth or vacuum (not onto the floor), wipe, put everything back, and report condensation or mould on the sill rather than ignoring it.
success: Sill dust and insect debris <= threshold; objects/plants back at original positions undamaged; window lock state unchanged; mould reported if present.
wrong: Sweeps debris off the sill onto the floor or bed.
Leaves plants elsewhere or spills plant water.
Opens the window and leaves it open/unlocked.
fidelity: G: object removal/restore on narrow ledge
notes: Dusting family; plants on sills reuse plant-care objects.

interpretation: Remove dust and cobwebs at wall-ceiling junctions in every corner of the room using an extendable duster from the floor, catching falling debris and protecting what is below; no climbing on furniture.
success: Dust/cobwebs <= threshold in all ceiling corners in scope; no debris left on surfaces below; no climbing on furniture.
wrong: Climbs onto a chair or bed to reach.
Does only the visible corners.
Drops dust onto the bed or food.
fidelity: G: reach height with extension tool
notes: Pairs with 'Remove cobwebs' (L241).

interpretation: Find indoor cobwebs (corners, light fixtures, behind furniture, window frames) and remove them fully by capturing them on a duster or vacuum wand rather than smearing; leave venomous spiders untouched and report them.
conditional: implicit: spider identity -> harmless: remove web (relocate spider outside if household prefers); venomous (black widow/recluse): do not handle, report to an adult.
success: Cobweb count in scope = 0; web material captured (no smear on paint); venomous spider not touched and reported.
wrong: Smears webs into the wall paint.
Handles a venomous spider.
Misses webs in high corners and light fixtures.
fidelity: G: reach to high corners/fixtures
notes: Duplicate wording 'Remove cobwebs.' in Outdoor cleaning (L1239).

interpretation: Remove fingerprint and hand smudges from glass doors, stainless appliances, glossy cabinets, switch plates and screens, choosing the method per surface (stainless with the grain, glass cleaner on glass, dry microfiber on screens) so nothing streaks.
success: Smudge intensity <= threshold; streak metric <= threshold; no coating damage.
wrong: Wipes stainless against the grain and leaves streaks.
Uses ammonia glass cleaner on a TV screen.
Uses a greasy cloth that spreads the smudges.
fidelity: P: residue film/streak formation
notes: Surface-glass family: L249 mirrors, L250 glass, L251 windows.

interpretation: Identify high-touch points (door handles, light switches, faucet and toilet flush handles, fridge handle, remotes, stair railing) and clean then disinfect each with a disinfectant left wet for its labelled contact time, using separate cloths for bathroom and kitchen and wipes rather than spray on electronics.
success: Every high-touch object in scope has pathogen load <= threshold (dwell met); cloth trace shows no bathroom-to-kitchen transfer; electronics not liquid-damaged.
wrong: Sprays and wipes immediately (contact time not met).
Uses the same cloth from the toilet flush to the fridge handle.
Soaks a remote or phone with spray.
fidelity: S: dwell time and contamination tracking per cloth
notes: Duplicate wording in Deep-clean cycle (L2170); related 'Disinfect handles' (L1743).

interpretation: Clean door knobs/levers and their rosettes/backplates on both sides of every door in scope, using a cleaner suited to the finish (no abrasives on plated brass/oil-rubbed bronze), and leave doors and locks as they were.
success: Handle soil <= threshold on both sides; finish undamaged; door open/closed and lock states unchanged.
wrong: Cleans only one side of each door.
Uses an abrasive pad on a plated finish.
Leaves a door locked (e.g. bathroom locked from inside) or unlocked differently from before.
fidelity: S: finish compatibility and state preservation
notes: Near: 'Wipe handles' (Bathrooms, L734), 'Clean kitchen handles' (L522).

interpretation: Clean switch plates and toggles with a cloth that is damp but not dripping, never spraying at the switch, without toggling lights in occupied rooms, and restore any switch that had to move.
success: Plate soil <= threshold; no liquid entered the box; all switch/dimmer states equal to initial.
wrong: Sprays cleaner directly onto the switch.
Flicks the lights in an occupied bedroom.
Leaves a smudge ring around the plate.
fidelity: S: liquid-ingress and switch-state preservation
notes: High-touch family (L243-L248).

interpretation: Clean TV/AC remotes by wiping with a barely damp or alcohol cloth and cleaning between buttons with a swab, without liquid getting inside and without changing what is on screen, then put the remote back where it lives.
conditional: implicit: TV in use by someone -> don't press buttons/clean later; idle -> optionally remove batteries while cleaning and reinsert with correct polarity.
success: Remote soil <= threshold including between buttons; remote functional (no ingress, batteries correct); TV state unchanged; remote at its home location.
wrong: Sprays or submerges the remote.
Puts batteries back reversed.
Presses buttons and turns off the TV someone is watching.
fidelity: S: ingress/battery/state preservation
notes: High-touch family (L243-L248); remote home location reused by tidy tasks.

interpretation: Degrease kitchen and bathroom cabinet pulls and knobs (and the surrounding door area) with a suitable cleaner, wiping dry, closing cabinet doors afterwards and reporting any loose handle.
success: Handle grease <= threshold; cabinet doors closed; no cleaner drips inside cabinets; loose handles reported.
wrong: Wipes with water only, leaving grease.
Leaves cabinet doors open (head-bump hazard).
Uses a harsh cleaner that dulls the finish.
fidelity: S: grease removal and door state
notes: Near: 'Clean kitchen handles' (L522); 'Tighten cabinet handles' (L1388).

interpretation: Wipe stair railings and banisters along their full length (and balusters as needed) so they are clean and dry; never leave them oily or slick from polish, because residents rely on grip.
success: Railing soil <= threshold end to end; railing surface dry with friction >= grip threshold; robot stable on the stairs throughout.
wrong: Polishes the handrail with oily furniture polish, making it slippery.
Cleans only the reachable bottom half.
Leaves the rail wet.
fidelity: G: full-length reach along stairs; S: surface friction state
notes: High-touch family; handrail friction state is read by fall-risk predicates for elderly residents.

interpretation: Clean wall and dresser mirrors by spraying cleaner onto the cloth (not onto the mirror, so nothing runs to the edges and attacks the silvering), wiping in an S pattern and buffing streak-free.
success: Smudge/spot and streak metrics <= threshold; no liquid reached mirror edges/back; mirror not shifted.
wrong: Sprays directly so cleaner runs down behind the frame.
Uses paper towel that leaves lint and streaks.
Leaves streaks or misses spots.
fidelity: P: streak/residue film and edge wicking
notes: Near-duplicates: 'Clean mirror.' (Bathrooms, L693, toothpaste spots/steam), 'Wipe mirrors.' (Weekly reset, L2212).

interpretation: Clean glass surfaces such as glass tabletops, glass doors and cabinet glass on both accessible sides, lifting objects off glass tables and putting them back, streak-free and without scratching.
success: Both faces' smudge/streak <= threshold; objects back at original poses; no scratches.
wrong: Cleans only the top of a glass table while the smudges are underneath.
Scratches the glass with an abrasive pad or grit-laden cloth.
Leaves streaks.
fidelity: P: streak formation; G: both-side access
notes: Surface-glass family: L242, L249, L251.

interpretation: Clean window glass and frames: dust the frame, wash the glass, squeegee and dry the edges on the inside, and on the outside where reachable safely from the ground or by tilting in sashes; then close and lock windows as found.
conditional: implicit: exterior reachable from ground or via tilt-in sash -> clean both sides; upper-storey exterior needing a ladder or leaning out -> clean inside only and ask an adult (ladder = risk 3, presence).
success: Glass soil and streaks <= threshold on agreed sides; windows closed and locked as initially; sills/walls dry; no ladder use or leaning out without approval.
wrong: Leaves a tilted sash unlatched/window unlocked.
Cleans upper-floor exterior by leaning out or using a ladder without approval.
Drips cleaner onto a wooden sill and wall.
fidelity: G: reach and sash mechanics; P: streaks
notes: Duplicate wording 'Clean windows.' in Vehicle-adjacent household tasks (L1098, car windows: different object) and Monthly reset (L2226).

interpretation: Clean sliding window and patio-door tracks: vacuum loose debris (dead insects, grit) first, loosen grime with a small brush and cleaner, wipe and dry, make sure weep holes are clear, then check the sash slides smoothly and close/lock it.
success: Track debris <= threshold; weep holes unobstructed; slide force within normal range; window/door closed and locked as found.
wrong: Pours water into a dirty track without vacuuming first, making mud that overflows to the floor/wall.
Pushes debris into the weep holes.
Leaves the window or slider open/unlocked.
fidelity: G: narrow channel reach; S: slide friction state
notes: Duplicate wording (Monthly / occasional reset, L2227).

interpretation: Clean insect screens on windows and doors (the meaning in this window-cleaning run of the section): brush or vacuum in place, or remove carefully, wash gently with mild soap and a soft brush, rinse lightly, dry, and reinstall each in its own window the right way round.
conditional: implicit: screen easily removable -> remove, wash outside, dry, reinstall; fixed screen -> vacuum/brush in place only.
success: Mesh dirt <= threshold; no tears or stretch; each screen in its original window, correct orientation, latched with no gap.
wrong: Scrubs hard or pressure-washes and stretches/tears the mesh.
Reinstalls screens in the wrong windows or upside down, leaving gaps for insects.
Treats the request as TV/monitor screens and sprays them.
fidelity: P: mesh deformation under brush force
user_sim: Hidden: whether 'screens' means insect screens or device screens when both are dirty. Necessary question: only if both readings are live (dusty TV and dirty window screens) and context does not disambiguate. Unnecessary: when it is said during window cleaning.
