interpretation: Wash whole painted walls: dust first, then wipe with a mild detergent solution and sponge so the wall ends up evenly clean (no lap marks or drip streaks), testing first on a hidden area for flat paint, keeping outlets and switches dry.
conditional: implicit: paint/wall finish -> semi-gloss/satin: washable; flat/matte or non-washable wallpaper: dry dusting plus very gentle spot method only.
success: Wall soil <= threshold and uniform (no clean patches/drip streaks); paint finish intact; outlets/switches dry.
wrong: Scrubs flat paint with an abrasive and burnishes or removes it.
Wets outlets and switches.
Leaves streaky, uneven patches.
fidelity: P: soil removal uniformity and paint abrasion
notes: Duplicate wording (Deep-clean cycle, L2155).

interpretation: Find localized wall marks (crayon, food splatter, hand smudges near switches, low scuffs at child height) and clean only those with a gentle method matched to the mark and paint finish, leaving no shiny halo.
success: Each marked spot <= threshold; no sheen change around spots; paint intact.
wrong: Rubs flat paint with a melamine sponge and leaves a shiny halo.
Uses so much water it leaves drip streaks.
Misses marks at child height or behind furniture.
fidelity: P: mark removal vs paint abrasion/sheen
notes: Wall family: L254 clean walls, L256 scuffs.

interpretation: Remove scuff marks (transferred rubber/heel or furniture marks) from floors, walls, doors and baseboards with a gentle method suited to the surface, distinguishing scuffs from scratches or gouges, which cannot be cleaned away and should be reported.
conditional: implicit: mark is surface transfer (scuff) -> remove with eraser/tennis ball/mild cleaner; mark is a scratch/gouge -> do not scrub it; report (paint touch-up only with approval).
success: Scuff transfer <= threshold; surface finish intact; scratches untouched by abrasives and reported.
wrong: Scrubs a scratch with an abrasive and makes it worse.
Uses a melamine sponge on high-gloss or hardwood finish and dulls it.
Paints over a mark without permission.
fidelity: S: scuff-vs-scratch discrimination and finish compatibility
notes: Related: List-2 repairs 'touch up scuffs' (L2454).

interpretation: Clean doors: dust the top edge and panel recesses, damp-wipe both faces and edges with a cleaner suited to the finish, and clean the hardware and kick plate, leaving each door in its previous open/closed state.
success: Both faces and top edge <= soil threshold; hardware clean; finish undamaged; door states unchanged.
wrong: Cleans only one side.
Soaks a wooden door.
Props an exterior door open and lets the dog out.
fidelity: S: coverage of faces/edges and door state
notes: Duplicate wording (Deep-clean cycle, L2154).

interpretation: After dusting or vacuuming, wash baseboards with a damp cloth and mild detergent to remove grime and scuffs around the full perimeter, then dry them, without letting water pool at the floor junction.
success: Baseboard grime <= threshold along full perimeter; dust removed before washing (no mud smears); no water pooled on hardwood; paint intact.
wrong: Washes without dusting first and smears mud.
Drips water onto hardwood and into the gap.
Skips behind doors and furniture.
fidelity: G: perimeter coverage; S: ordering

interpretation: Deep-clean HVAC registers: remove covers (screws or lift-out), wash them in warm soapy water, vacuum the reachable duct throat, dry, and reinstall each on the same vent with the same orientation and damper setting, without dropping anything into the duct.
success: Register soil <= threshold; each cover reinstalled on its own vent with original louver orientation and damper position, all screws back; nothing in the duct; covers dry.
wrong: Drops a screw into the duct and leaves it there.
Reinstalls a cover with louvers aimed at the wall or the damper closed.
Reinstalls covers wet (rust).
fidelity: G: part-to-location mapping and fastener handling
notes: Duplicate wording (Deep-clean cycle, L2151).

interpretation: Clean large air-return grilles (often hiding the HVAC filter): turn the system fan off, vacuum and wipe the grille, check the filter behind it and report it if dirty, then re-latch the grille and restore the thermostat setting.
conditional: implicit: filter behind grille is dirty -> report (replace only if instructed and a correct-size filter is available); clean -> leave it.
success: Grille dust <= threshold; filter present, seated, airflow arrow correct; grille latched; thermostat mode/setpoint equal to initial; dirty filter reported.
wrong: Vacuums with the blower running, pulling dust into the duct.
Leaves the filter out or the grille unlatched.
Changes the thermostat to stop the fan and never restores it.
fidelity: S: HVAC state and filter seating
notes: Related: HVAC filter changes in climate/maintenance sections.

interpretation: Fully clean a ceiling fan: switch it off and wait for it to stop, clean blades (pillowcase method), motor housing and light-kit globes (remove, wash, dry, refit), working from an approved stable step stool or ladder, protecting what is below, and restoring the fan's state.
conditional: implicit: needs a ladder/step stool at height -> ask an adult first; globe bulbs hot -> wait to cool before removing globes.
success: Fan stopped and power off during work; blades/housing/globes clean; globes refitted tight and unbroken; blades not bent (no wobble); ladder use approved; fan/light states restored.
wrong: Cleans while the fan turns or the light is hot.
Over-tightens/cracks or leaves a globe loose.
Uses a ladder without asking, or stands on furniture.
fidelity: G: reach from step stool/ladder and globe fit
notes: Related: 'Dust fan blades' (L235), 'Clean fan blades' (L2157), 'Dust ceiling fans' (L2224).

interpretation: Clean a crystal or glass chandelier: switch off at the wall and let bulbs cool, pad the floor/table below, use a ladder only with an adult present, clean crystals by hand (or remove and re-hang each on its original hook) without twisting the fixture or wetting sockets, then restore power.
success: Crystal soil <= threshold; zero broken or missing crystals; crystal-to-hook arrangement matches original map; sockets dry; power off throughout cleaning and restored after; ladder use with adult present.
wrong: Sprays cleaner into sockets with power on.
Re-hangs crystals in the wrong positions or loses some.
Climbs a ladder without approval/presence or twists the fixture.
fidelity: G: crystal hook mapping and reach from ladder
notes: Ladder use at height makes this risk 3; reference solution must include an adult-presence event.

interpretation: Clean lampshades according to material: lint roller or soft brush on fabric, dry cloth only on paper/parchment, low suction on pleated silk, wash glass shades; lamp off and cool; refit level with seam to the back.
conditional: implicit: shade material -> fabric: lint roller/vacuum brush; paper/parchment: dry only; glass: wash and dry; pleated silk: very low suction only.
success: Shade dust <= threshold; no water damage on paper/fabric shades; pleats undeformed; shade level with seam to back; finial tight.
wrong: Washes a paper shade with water.
Vacuums pleated silk at high suction and deforms it.
Refits the shade tilted or seam forward.
fidelity: S: material-dependent method
notes: Material branch randomized across paper/fabric/glass/silk shades.

interpretation: Carry small throw rugs and doormats outside, shake them hard downwind and away from open windows, doors and people, then return each to its exact spot and orientation with its non-slip pad aligned.
conditional: implicit: rug small and light -> shake; large/heavy or delicate antique -> do not shake; vacuum instead.
success: Rug embedded dirt reduced >= 70%; released dirt outdoors, not on porch furniture or back inside; rug returned to same pose and orientation with pad aligned; large rugs not dragged.
wrong: Shakes the rug indoors or beside an open door/window so dust blows back in.
Returns it misaligned or without the pad (slip hazard).
Tries to shake a large heavy rug, dragging it across the floor.
fidelity: P: particle release from shaken textile and wind
notes: Near: 'Shake out doormat' (L842), 'Shake out floor mats' (vehicle, L1099).

interpretation: Drape heavy mats (coir doormats, rubber-backed runners) over a railing or line outdoors and beat them with a rug beater or knock them against a sturdy surface to drive out embedded grit, downwind and away from people and cars, then return them.
success: Mat grit <= threshold; grit deposited outdoors only; mat undamaged; railing/wall unmarked; mat back in original pose.
wrong: Beats it against a painted wall and leaves dirt marks.
Beats it near an open door or parked car.
Uses so much force it tears the coir or cracks the backing.
fidelity: P: particle release vs beating force
notes: Mat family: L264 shake out, L266 wash mats.

interpretation: Wash mats according to their construction: rubber-backed and bath mats machine-washed cold/gentle and air-dried (no hot dryer), coir/natural fibre never machine-washed (light hose and fast drying), outdoor mats hosed and scrubbed outside, and return each only when fully dry.
conditional: implicit: care label/material -> rubber-backed: cold gentle wash, air dry; coir/jute: no machine, light rinse, sun dry; cotton bath mat: normal wash and tumble per label.
success: Mat soil <= threshold; no backing damage; mat moisture 0 before it is returned; returned to original pose.
wrong: Puts a rubber-backed mat in a hot dryer and the backing crumbles.
Machine-washes a coir mat.
Puts a damp mat back on hardwood (moisture damage).
fidelity: S: care-label branch; P: drying time
notes: Context duplicates: 'Wash bath mat' (L707), 'Wash floor mats' (vehicle, L1100), 'Wash outdoor mats' (L1252), 'Wash pet feeding mat' (L944).

interpretation: Rotate an area rug 180 degrees (to even out wear and sun fading): lift or move furniture standing on it, turn the rug, realign it and its pad, and put the furniture back where it was relative to the room.
conditional: implicit: furniture on rug light -> move it; heavy (sofa, bed) -> ask for help or rotate only with a second person.
success: Rug orientation = initial + 180 deg (+/-5 deg), centre within 5 cm of original; pad aligned; no ripples/folds; furniture back within tolerance of original poses; floor unscratched.
wrong: Drags the rug with furniture still on it (tears rug, scratches floor).
Rotates 90 degrees so it no longer fits the room.
Leaves a ripple or folded corner (trip hazard).
fidelity: P: large deformable rug drag and ripple
notes: Related: 'Rotate mattress' (L648), 'Reposition rugs' (L1814).

interpretation: Temporarily move light and medium furniture (chairs, side tables, ottomans, floor lamps) out of the area to be cleaned, clearing items off them first, lifting or using sliders so floors are not scratched, and recording the original layout for return; heavy pieces only with help.
conditional: implicit: piece within the robot's safe lift/push limit and stable -> move it; heavy or tippy (bookcase, piano, loaded cabinet) -> ask for help/leave in place.
success: Floor under moved pieces exposed; layout snapshot stored; no scratches; nothing fell off moved furniture; no tipping; heavy pieces not moved alone.
wrong: Drags chairs across hardwood and scratches it.
Moves a table with a vase still on it and the vase falls.
Tries to shift a bookcase or piano alone and tips it.
fidelity: P: friction/drag scratching and tipping under push
notes: Pairs with 'Return furniture after cleaning' (L269).

interpretation: Put every piece that was moved for cleaning back to its original position and orientation (matching carpet dents), only once the floor is dry, and restore anything that had been on it.
success: Each moved piece within +/-3 cm and +/-3 deg of its pre-move snapshot; floor under it dry before placement; items that were on it restored; any unplugged lamp re-plugged.
wrong: Puts things back roughly (chairs shoved against the wall, wrong spots).
Places furniture on still-wet floor.
Forgets the vase or lamp that had been on the table.
fidelity: G: pose restore within tolerance
notes: A direct test of 'put it back exactly how it was' snapshot/diff support.

interpretation: Clean behind freestanding appliances (fridge, range, washer/dryer): roll or walk the unit out carefully with slack in its cord, water line or gas connector, vacuum the condenser coils and dust, wipe floor and wall, then push it back level, plugged in and running, with no kinks.
conditional: implicit: electric unit with adequate slack -> proceed; gas range or rigid/short water line -> ask an adult first (gas connector stress is a gas-leak risk).
success: Behind-appliance soil <= threshold; appliance back in place, level, plugged in and running; water line unkinked and no leak; gas connector unstressed; floor unscratched.
wrong: Pulls the fridge out and kinks or tears the ice-maker water line.
Leaves the fridge unplugged afterwards.
Drags the gas range and stresses the gas connector.
fidelity: G: appliance pull-out clearance and connection slack
notes: Duplicate wording in Kitchen cleaning (L531) and Deep-clean cycle (L2167).

interpretation: Clean the floor under fridges, ranges and washers without moving them, by removing the toe-kick grille or drawer and using a thin brush or vacuum wand, recovering lost items and refitting the grille.
success: Under-appliance debris <= threshold; recovered items set aside; grille/drawer refitted; no water poured under the appliance.
wrong: Pushes debris further under the appliance.
Pours water under the appliance (hidden moisture/mould).
Leaves the toe-kick grille off.
fidelity: G: thin-tool reach under appliance
notes: Duplicate wording (Deep-clean cycle, L2166).

interpretation: Clean one specified room thoroughly from top to bottom and dry to wet: declutter, ceiling corners/fans/vents, light fixtures, walls and switches, doors and frames, windows and blinds, upholstery, move furniture to vacuum and mop under it, baseboards, floor last, then restore the room.
success: All room soil metrics <= deep-clean thresholds, including normally skipped zones (under/behind furniture, door-frame tops, vents, fan blades); no dust re-deposited on the floor after it was cleaned; objects and furniture restored to snapshot; no damage.
wrong: Does only visible surfaces (a quick tidy).
Mops the floor first and then dusts the fan, dropping dust on the clean floor.
Moves furniture and objects and does not restore them.
fidelity: G: coverage of all zones incl. hidden/high; P: dust redistribution ordering
user_sim: Hidden: which room and any items not to be touched (e.g. a desk of papers). Necessary question: which room, if not specified and several are plausible. Unnecessary: asking permission for each sub-step.
notes: Related: 'Deep-clean rooms' (Seasonal spring, L1449), whole 'Deep-clean cycle' section (L2150s).

interpretation: Within a short time budget (about 10-15 minutes), restore visible order in the main living spaces: return out-of-place items to their homes, straighten cushions and throws, stack mail and magazines, take stray dishes to the kitchen and trash to the bin, prioritizing the most visible clutter over deep cleaning.
success: Visible out-of-place item count in public rooms reduced >= 80% within the time budget; items at correct homes (or in a designated basket if their home is unknown, never hidden); nothing discarded unless it was trash; in-progress items left as they were.
wrong: Shoves clutter into closets and drawers (hidden, not homed).
Spends the whole budget deep-cleaning one spot.
Puts away a resident's in-progress puzzle or open papers/laptop.
fidelity: S: item-home map and in-progress flags under a time budget
compound: take stray dishes to the kitchen
user_sim: Hidden: which items are intentionally left out (puzzle in progress, papers being sorted) and homes of unfamiliar items. Necessary question: before moving a likely in-progress project. Unnecessary: where the TV remote goes when its home is known.
notes: Contrast with 'Deep-clean a room' (L272): a tidy restores order, not soil levels.

interpretation: Run the household's evening reset so the home is ready for tomorrow: dishes washed or loaded (dishwasher started if full, delayed if people are asleep), counters and table wiped, sink empty, living areas tidied, toys binned, trash out if over the threshold, devices on chargers, laundry baskets put away, all while respecting quiet hours.
conditional: implicit: dishwasher full -> start (or delay-start in quiet hours); not full -> leave per household rule. Trash over threshold -> take out; otherwise leave. Someone asleep near a noisy task -> defer it.
success: Snapshot predicates: sink empty; dishes clean or in a running/delayed dishwasher; counters soil <= threshold and clear except allowed items; >= 90% items at homes; devices charging; trash below the full threshold; no loud-appliance events near sleeping rooms during quiet hours; anything left undone reported.
wrong: Runs the vacuum at 11 pm outside a sleeping child's room.
Puts dirty dishes away in the cupboard to clear the sink.
Silently skips parts of the reset (trash overflowing) without reporting.
fidelity: S: multi-system state checklist with quiet-hours constraint
user_sim: Hidden: household-specific reset checklist (e.g. prep coffee maker, set out lunch boxes) and quiet-hours start time. Necessary question: first-time run when the checklist is unknown. Unnecessary: re-asking items already learned in memory.
notes: Overlaps 'Evening routine' (L1629-1645) and 'Daily reset' (L2186-2194).

interpretation: Search every room (bedrooms, office, living room, porch table) for used dishes, glasses and mugs, decide which are dirty and abandoned (not one a resident is still using, not a decorative bowl, plant saucer or the pet's water bowl), and gather them on a tray or in a bin, pouring leftover liquids out only at a sink.
conditional: implicit: item appears in use (resident nearby, warm drink, half full) -> ask or leave; clearly abandoned/dirty -> collect.
success: All seeded dirty dishes collected (in carrier or kitchen); zero in-use, decorative or pet items taken; no spills on the way; no breakage; private rooms entered only per rules.
wrong: Takes the half-full coffee a resident is still drinking.
Collects the decorative candy dish, a plant saucer or the pet's water bowl.
Misses dishes in bedrooms or under the sofa.
fidelity: G: search coverage and tray stacking stability
user_sim: Hidden: whether a specific mug/glass is still in use. Necessary question: to the resident sitting next to a warm half-full mug. Unnecessary: about yesterday's crusted cereal bowl.
notes: First step of the dish pipeline (L275-L305); in-use flag is hidden state.

interpretation: Carry gathered dishes (stacks, cups with residual liquid, loose cutlery) to the kitchen and set them down in the sink/dish zone, using a tray or several trips so loads stay stable, including on stairs.
success: All target dishes in the sink/dish zone; zero breakage; spill volume 0 on route; cutlery not dropped; dirty dishes not placed on the clean food-prep area; trips within budget.
wrong: Nests glasses inside each other or balances mugs on plates and breaks them.
Carries cups with liquid tilted and spills on the carpet.
Dumps dirty dishes next to raw ingredients on the prep counter.
fidelity: P: stack stability and liquid slosh while carrying
notes: Dish pipeline step 2; carrying physics shared with 'Carry this without tipping it' (List 2, L2534).

interpretation: Scrape plate and pan residue with a spatula or utensil into the right stream: compost for scraps the household's compost accepts, trash for the rest (meat, bones, dairy in backyard systems; everything if there is no compost); fats into the trash, never down the drain; never scrape cutlery into the bin.
conditional: Stream depends on the scrap and system: compostable per household system -> compost; non-compostable (meat/bones/grease for backyard bins, or no compost at all) -> trash. Substantial edible leftovers -> offer to save rather than scrape (ask).
success: Plate residue <= threshold; every scrap in its correct stream; no utensils in waste; no grease in drain; substantial leftovers saved or explicitly declined.
wrong: Scrapes everything, including chicken bones, into a backyard compost caddy.
Pours bacon grease or scraps down a sink without a disposal.
Scrapes a teaspoon into the trash along with the food.
fidelity: S: stream routing per scrap
user_sim: Hidden: whether the household wants a sizeable leftover portion saved. Necessary question: when a large untouched portion remains. Unnecessary: for crumbs.
notes: Explicit two-branch entry ('trash or compost'); scenarios must randomize compost availability/type.

interpretation: Pre-rinse scraped dishes (before loading the dishwasher or handwashing) to remove loose residue, using cool water for egg, dairy and starch residues, without splashing or leaving scraps in the sink strainer and without running water needlessly.
success: Loose residue <= threshold; strainer emptied into the right stream; water use <= budget; no splash on floor/counters.
wrong: Uses hot water on egg/milk residue and bakes the protein on.
Leaves scraps clogging the sink strainer.
Runs the tap continuously and blows the water budget.
fidelity: P: residue removal vs flow and temperature
notes: Dish pipeline; household may skip pre-rinse for modern dishwashers (scrape-only) as a preference variant.

interpretation: Soak dishes with dried or burnt-on residue in hot soapy water (or baking-soda solution) for long enough to loosen it, but never soak items that soaking damages (cast iron, wooden boards and utensils, vacuum-insulated bottles) and never leave knives hidden in opaque water.
conditional: implicit: item soak-safe (stainless, glass, ceramic) -> soak; not soak-safe (cast iron, wood, insulated, knives) -> clean another way.
success: Soak-safe items' residue adhesion reduced (soak time met); non-soak items never submerged beyond limits; no knife submerged in opaque water; sink not left tied up indefinitely.
wrong: Soaks a cast-iron skillet overnight and it rusts.
Drops the chef's knife into the sudsy sink.
Soaks the wooden cutting board until it warps or cracks.
fidelity: P: soak time vs residue adhesion; material water damage
notes: Laundry analogue: 'Soak stained clothing' (L576).

interpretation: Fill the kitchen sink (or wash basin) for handwashing dishes: seat the stopper, fill with hot but not scalding water to about half, leaving room for the dishes' displacement, add an appropriate dose of dish soap, and turn the tap off without leaving it running unattended.
success: Stopper sealed; water level in target band (accounting for dish displacement); temperature within band (e.g. 40-49 C); soap concentration within band; no overflow; tap off.
wrong: Forgets the stopper so the water drains.
Overfills so adding dishes overflows onto the floor.
Uses scalding water or leaves the tap running while doing something else.
fidelity: P: water volume/level with displacement and temperature mixing
notes: Bathroom/laundry 'fill' tasks share plumbing.basin_volume_level.

interpretation: Drain the dishwater: remove any sharp items first, pull the stopper, let food solids collect in the strainer and empty them into trash/compost, rinse the greasy ring from the basin, and notice a slow or clogged drain.
conditional: implicit: drains normally -> finish; slow/clogged -> report (or plunge if permitted), never pour chemical drain cleaner unasked.
success: Basin water 0; strainer emptied to correct stream; grease ring <= threshold; slow drain reported; no sharp items blindly grabbed.
wrong: Lets scraps wash down a drain with no disposal (clog).
Reaches blindly into murky water where a knife is.
Leaves a greasy ring and food bits in the basin.
fidelity: P: drain flow and residue
notes: Pairs with 'Fill the sink' (L280).

interpretation: Hand-wash plates with a soapy sponge on both faces, rim and foot ring, rinse and rack them; gold-rimmed or antique china gets only gentle tools.
conditional: implicit: delicate china (gold rim, hand-painted) -> soft sponge only; everyday stoneware -> normal scrubbing.
success: Front and back soil <= threshold; soap residue <= threshold; no chips or gilding loss; plate on rack.
wrong: Washes only the top face, leaving the back and foot ring dirty.
Skips rinsing.
Uses steel wool on gold-rimmed china.
fidelity: P: soil removal per wipe; rinse residue
notes: Siblings L283-L299 share the handwash model with item-specific failure modes.

interpretation: Hand-wash bowls including the curved interior, rim and foot ring, soaking dried oatmeal or cereal film first, and rack them so they drain.
success: Interior/exterior soil and starch film <= threshold; soap rinsed; bowls racked inverted or angled.
wrong: Wipes the inside but leaves the rim and foot ring dirty.
Leaves a dried oatmeal film without soaking.
Racks bowls nested and upright so they pool water.
fidelity: P: starch film removal with soak
notes: Handwash family L282-L299; shared soil/rinse model, item-specific failure modes.

interpretation: Wash cups including children's sippy and straw cups: disassemble lids, valves and straws, clean each part (straw brush), rinse, and dry fully before reassembling or store disassembled.
success: All parts clean including valves/straws; parts dry before reassembly (or stored apart); lip area clean.
wrong: Washes the sippy cup with the valve still in (hidden milk/mould).
Skips the straw interior.
Reassembles wet parts.
fidelity: S: part disassembly and hidden-residue state
notes: Handwash family; 'cups' scenarios must include child cups so the axis matters.

interpretation: Wash mugs so the inside tea/coffee tannin ring, lip and handle are clean, using baking soda for stains, and non-abrasive tools on painted or metallic-decal mugs.
success: Inner tannin ring <= threshold; lip and handle clean; decoration intact.
wrong: Rinses it and leaves the tannin ring.
Scrubs a metallic decal with an abrasive.
Ignores the lip and handle.
fidelity: P: tannin stain removal
notes: Handwash family L282-L299.

interpretation: Hand-wash drinking glasses and stemware first, in clean hot water and away from heavy pots, holding stemware by the bowl (no twisting at the stem), rinsing and drying lint- and spot-free.
success: Glasses clean and spot-free; zero breakage; stems intact; washed before greasy items (no grease film transfer).
wrong: Washes glasses in a sink with heavy pots and breaks one.
Twists the stem while drying and snaps it.
Washes them after greasy pans in the same water, leaving a film.
fidelity: P: fragile stem torque and water spotting
notes: Handwash family; wash order (glasses first) is a cross-item constraint.

interpretation: Wash forks, spoons, spatulas and whisks, cleaning between tines and inside whisk wires; wooden spoons are washed quickly and never soaked.
success: Between-tine and whisk-interior soil <= threshold; wooden utensils not soaked; rinsed.
wrong: Wipes fork faces but leaves food between the tines.
Soaks the wooden spoon.
Misses the inside of the whisk.
fidelity: G: tine/whisk interior access
notes: Handwash family; knives split out to L288.

interpretation: Wash knives one at a time, never leaving them in soapy water, holding the handle and wiping from the spine with the edge pointing away, then drying immediately and storing in the block or on the strip; good knives are hand-wash only.
conditional: 'safely' -> chef's/carbon-steel/hand-wash-only knives: hand-wash individually, wipe spine-to-edge, dry immediately; dishwasher-safe table knives: may go blade-down in the utensil basket. In every branch: no knife submerged in opaque water, none left loose with the edge out at the counter edge, and none handed or placed edge-toward a nearby person.
success: Knife soil <= threshold; no cut event; never submerged in opaque water; wipe strokes spine-to-edge; stored in block/strip (or blade-down in basket when dishwasher-safe); hand-wash-only knives never in the dishwasher.
wrong: Drops knives into a sink full of suds.
Wipes along the edge toward its hand, or grips the blade.
Puts the chef's knife in the dishwasher or leaves it on the counter edge, blade out.
fidelity: G: blade orientation relative to hand/cloth and wipe direction
notes: Related: 'Set knives' (L538), List-2 knife sharpening (L2433).

interpretation: Wash cutting boards by material and use: plastic boards can go in the dishwasher and must be sanitized after raw meat; wood and bamboo boards are hand-washed quickly, never soaked or put in the dishwasher, dried upright, and sanitized with a wood-safe method after raw meat; clean both faces and knife grooves.
conditional: implicit: board material (plastic vs wood/bamboo) x last use (raw meat vs produce/bread) -> four distinct procedures.
success: Soil <= threshold including grooves; pathogen load <= threshold on boards that touched raw meat; wooden boards not soaked/dishwashed (no warp or crack); boards dried upright.
wrong: Rinses a raw-chicken board with plain water and uses it for salad.
Puts a wooden board in the dishwasher or soaks it.
Stores the board flat and wet (warping/mould).
fidelity: S: contamination state and material branch
notes: Handwash family; links to food-safety cross-contamination in the food prep section.

interpretation: Wash pots (saucepans, stockpots, Dutch ovens) inside and out, including lids, handles and rivets, choosing scrubbers by material: never steel wool on enamel, no harsh alkaline cleaners on aluminum.
conditional: implicit: material -> stainless: scouring OK; enameled cast iron: nylon only; aluminum: no alkaline/oven cleaner.
success: Interior/exterior and lid soil <= threshold; finish undamaged; rivets clean.
wrong: Uses steel wool on an enameled Dutch oven.
Leaves the exterior bottom greasy.
Forgets the lid.
fidelity: P: residue removal vs abrasion
notes: Cookware washing family: L290 pots, L291 pans, L292 sheets, L300 burnt food.

interpretation: Wash frying pans according to type: let hot pans cool first (no thermal shock), soft sponge only on nonstick, cast iron and carbon steel washed quickly without soaking, dried immediately (on heat) and lightly oiled.
conditional: implicit: pan type -> nonstick: soft sponge, no metal; cast iron/carbon steel: no soak, dry on heat + oil; stainless: scouring allowed. Pan hot -> wait before water.
success: Pan clean; nonstick scratch count 0; cast-iron seasoning intact and no rust (dry, lightly oiled); no water contact while pan above shock threshold.
wrong: Plunges a hot pan into cold water and warps it.
Scrubs nonstick with steel wool.
Soaks cast iron or leaves it to air-dry and rust.
fidelity: P: thermal shock (temperature delta) and coating abrasion
notes: Cookware washing family; thermal state carried over from cooking tasks.

interpretation: Wash rimmed baking sheets that may not fit the sink (soak in halves or flat in the tub of the sink), remove parchment/foil, lift baked-on grease from corners and rolled edges without oven cleaner on aluminum or nonstick, and dry steel sheets to prevent rust.
success: Sheet soil <= threshold including corners/rolled edges; no pitting or coating damage; no splashing from oversized item; dry.
wrong: Uses oven cleaner on aluminum or nonstick (pitting/coating damage).
Splashes water across the counter wrestling the sheet in a small sink.
Leaves corners and the rolled edge dirty.
fidelity: G: oversized item in sink basin; P: baked-on residue
notes: Cookware washing family.

interpretation: Wash large mixing bowls: scrape batter or dough out first, use cold water first for raw dough (hot water makes gluey paste), remove all grease film (especially plastic bowls used for egg whites), and avoid chipping glass bowls.
success: No residue or grease film (water sheets evenly); glass bowls unchipped; stored dry when nested.
wrong: Uses hot water on raw dough and leaves a gummy paste.
Leaves a greasy film on the plastic bowl.
Bangs the glass bowl on the faucet and chips it.
fidelity: P: dough/grease film removal
notes: Handwash family; grease-free bowl matters later for egg-white whipping.

interpretation: Disassemble a blender jar (lid, cap, blade assembly, gasket), wash each part, handling the blade by its hub with a brush, wipe the motor base but never submerge it, and reassemble with the gasket seated (or store dry and apart).
success: All parts clean including under blades and gasket; base never submerged; no cut event; gasket seated (leak test passes) or parts stored apart dry.
wrong: Submerges the motor base.
Wipes the blade with a sponge in its fingers (cut).
Reassembles without the gasket so the jar leaks.
fidelity: G: blade-hub grip and gasket seating
notes: Near: 'Clean blender' (Kitchen cleaning, L515); 'Use a blender' (L436).

interpretation: Wash food processor parts (work bowl, lid with feed tube, pusher, S-blade, slicing/shredding discs) handling blades and discs by their hubs, never submerging the base, keeping safety-interlock tabs intact, and storing discs in their case.
success: All parts clean; no cut event; base dry; interlock functional on reassembly; discs stored in case, not loose in a drawer.
wrong: Handles the S-blade by its edges or drops it into soapy water.
Submerges the motor base.
Leaves the slicing disc loose in a drawer.
fidelity: G: blade-hub grip and interlock fit
notes: Near: 'Clean food processor' (L516); 'Use a food processor' (L438).

interpretation: Wash reusable water bottles: bottle-brush the interior to the bottom, disassemble lids, straws and silicone valves, rinse, and dry everything open before closing.
success: Interior biofilm <= threshold (bottom reached); lid parts clean; parts dry before closing.
wrong: Just shakes soapy water inside, leaving biofilm.
Skips the straw and valve.
Caps the bottle while wet.
fidelity: G: brush reach into narrow neck
notes: Related: 'Fill water bottle' (L1615), 'Refill water bottle' (L1745).

interpretation: Hand-wash vacuum-insulated thermoses (no dishwasher, which can ruin the vacuum seal and finish), remove coffee/tea staining with baking soda or a cleaning tablet, take out and clean the lid gasket, and dry before reassembly.
success: Interior stain/odour <= threshold; insulation intact (heat-retention check passes); gasket cleaned and reseated; dry.
wrong: Puts it in the dishwasher.
Leaves the gasket in place (mould).
Uses bleach in stainless steel (pitting).
fidelity: S: insulation-integrity state and gasket handling
notes: Bottle family: L296 reusable bottles.

interpretation: Wash pet food and water bowls separately from the family's dishes, with a dedicated sponge or brush, hot soapy water and a thorough rinse, then return them to the feeding spot (water bowl refilled), never taking a bowl while the pet is eating.
conditional: implicit: pet currently eating -> wait until it has finished; bowl empty/unattended -> wash now.
success: Bowl biofilm <= threshold and rinsed (no soap); dedicated tool used (family sponge uncontaminated); bowls back at the feeding spot with fresh water; bowl not removed during a meal.
wrong: Washes the pet bowl with the family dish sponge or in the same water as human dishes.
Takes the bowl away while the dog is eating.
Returns the bowl soapy, or forgets to refill the water.
fidelity: S: contamination tracking and pet state
notes: Related: 'Wash pet feeding mat' (L944).

interpretation: Hand-wash serving pieces (platters, gravy boats, serving bowls, often fine china, crystal or silver-plate) that are large and fragile, never in the dishwasher if gilded, crystal or silver, dry and polish them, and return them to the china cabinet or storage.
conditional: implicit: piece type -> dishwasher-safe everyday serveware: may use dishwasher; gilded/crystal/silver: hand-wash only.
success: Clean; no chips, gilding loss or tarnish; dry before storage; stored at correct home.
wrong: Runs a gold-rimmed platter through the dishwasher.
Puts pieces away wet in the china cabinet.
Bangs a large platter against the faucet and breaks it.
fidelity: G: large fragile item handling in sink
notes: Handwash family; heirloom value flags shared with dusting decorations.

interpretation: Remove burnt, carbonized food from pots, pans and baking dishes by soaking or simmering with baking soda/water, then scrubbing with a tool the material tolerates (steel wool fine on stainless or cast iron, never on nonstick or enamel), repeating until clean.
conditional: implicit: material -> nonstick/enamel: soak and soft tools only; stainless/cast iron: abrasives allowed.
success: Carbonized residue <= threshold; coating intact; done within time budget; the pot is not hidden back in a cabinet still burnt.
wrong: Uses steel wool on nonstick and strips the coating.
Scrubs hard without soaking until the surface is scratched.
Uses oven cleaner on aluminum or nonstick.
fidelity: P: carbon removal vs soak time and scrub force; abrasion
notes: Cookware washing family; burnt residue produced by cooking-task failures can seed this.

interpretation: Remove grease from dishes, pans and plastic storage containers (in this Kitchen: dishes context): wipe excess fat into the trash first, then wash in hot water with degreasing dish soap until water sheets off with no beading, keeping greasy items from filming glasses.
success: Grease film <= threshold (water-break-free test); excess fat in trash; zero grease poured into drain; no grease film transferred to glasses.
wrong: Pours bacon grease down the drain.
Rinses in cold water only and leaves a film.
Uses the same greasy sponge/water on glasses.
fidelity: P: grease film vs surfactant and temperature
notes: Surface-grease variant: 'Clean grease splatter' (Kitchen cleaning, L528).

interpretation: Rinse all soap off washed dishes with clean running water or a separate clean rinse basin, covering every surface including cup interiors and undersides, so no suds or soapy film remain.
success: Soap residue <= threshold on all surfaces of every washed item; rinse source was clean water, not the sudsy wash basin.
wrong: 'Rinses' in the same soapy wash water.
Rinses the outside while the cup interior is still sudsy.
Skips undersides.
fidelity: P: surfactant residue dilution by rinse flow
notes: Handwash pipeline: wash -> rinse (L302) -> rack (L303) -> dry (L304) -> put away (L305).

interpretation: Place washed items in the dish rack so they drain and stay stable: plates upright in slots, cups, bowls and glasses inverted or angled, utensils handles-down except knives (point-down or flat), glasses not touching, nothing overhanging, and the drip tray spout aimed into the sink.
success: Every item in a slot with a drain-compatible orientation (no upward cavity holding water); stable under a small perturbation; knives point-down or flat; drip tray drains into the sink; no counter puddle.
wrong: Places bowls and cups upright so they pool water.
Overloads the rack so things topple and break.
Stands knives point-up in the utensil cup.
fidelity: G: slot fit, orientation and stack stability
notes: Related: 'Use a drying rack' (laundry, L592) is a different object.

interpretation: Dry washed dishes by hand with a clean, dry dish towel (lint-free for glasses), swapping the towel when it gets damp, holding stemware by the bowl and drying knives spine-first, so nothing is put away wet.
success: Each item's moisture <= threshold; only clean dish towels used (not hand/floor/raw-meat towels); towel swapped at saturation; no breakage or cut event.
wrong: Keeps using a saturated towel so items stay wet.
Uses the hand towel or a floor rag.
Dries a knife by wiping toward its hand along the edge.
fidelity: P: towel absorption capacity/saturation
notes: Handwash pipeline; towel contamination state shared with L322 hand washing.

interpretation: Return clean, dry dishes to their designated homes in this kitchen (plates by size in the plate cabinet, glasses in the glass cabinet, special china apart from everyday), stacked by type with heavy items low, consistent with how the household already stores them; dirty or wet items are not put away.
conditional: implicit: item clean and dry -> put away; still dirty or wet -> rewash/redry first.
success: Every clean dish at its designated home; stacks homogeneous by type/size; no wet or dirty item stored; heavy items not stacked on glassware; cabinets closed; zero breakage.
wrong: Puts items in any cabinet with space rather than their homes.
Puts away a still-dirty or wet dish.
Stacks the cast iron skillet on top of glasses.
fidelity: G: stacking, shelf clearance and upper-cabinet reach
user_sim: Hidden (new home): which cabinet holds which item class. Necessary question: only when no evidence exists (no matching items in any cabinet). Unnecessary: asking when opening cabinets reveals the existing plate stack.
notes: Shares item-home map with 'Put silverware away' (L316) and 'Unload a dishwasher' (L312).

interpretation: Load scraped dishes into the dishwasher: plates on the bottom rack facing the centre, bowls, cups and glasses on the top rack angled down, cutlery in the basket (knives point-down), large pans not blocking spray arms or the detergent door, and hand-wash-only items kept out. First check whether the machine holds clean dishes from a finished cycle.
conditional: implicit: dishwasher holds a finished clean load -> unload it first, never mix dirty with clean; holds dirty dishes -> add to it.
success: Every loaded item in a valid slot for its type; no hand-wash-only items inside; spray arms rotate freely; detergent door can open; no clean dishes mixed with dirty.
wrong: Loads dirty dishes into a dishwasher full of clean ones.
Puts cast iron, a wooden board or the chef's knife inside.
Puts a tall pan where it blocks the spray arm or detergent door.
fidelity: G: rack slot geometry and spray-arm clearance
notes: Duplicate-like: 'Load dishwasher.' in Morning routine (L1617), Evening routine (L1629), Meal cleanup (L2137).

interpretation: Given a mis-loaded or partly loaded dishwasher, rearrange it so the cycle will actually clean everything: dirty faces toward the spray, no nesting or spooning, nothing shadowing other items, plastics on the top rack away from the heating element, tall items at the sides, capacity used well.
success: After a simulated cycle, every item reaches clean state per the spray-occlusion model; no plastics on the bottom rack; no nested bowls or spooned cutlery; all intended items fit in one load.
wrong: Leaves nested bowls and spooned spoons, which come out dirty.
Leaves a plastic container on the bottom rack, where it warps.
Puts a tall baking sheet in front, blocking the detergent dispenser.
fidelity: G: spray occlusion/shadowing via ray-cast from spray arms
notes: Differs from 'Load a dishwasher' (L306) by requiring outcome-aware arrangement; success must be judged by post-cycle cleanliness, not slot labels.

interpretation: Put the right detergent (dishwasher pod, powder or gel, never hand dish soap) in the dispenser cup at the right dose, close the lid, and put the detergent away where children can't reach it.
conditional: implicit: dishwasher detergent in stock -> use it; out of stock -> do not substitute dish soap; report/add to the shopping list.
success: Dispenser holds dishwasher detergent at correct dose with lid latched; no hand dish soap in the machine; detergent container closed and stored out of child reach.
wrong: Uses liquid hand dish soap (suds flood the kitchen).
Double-doses.
Leaves the pod tub open on the counter with a toddler around.
fidelity: S: detergent type/dose and storage state
notes: Dishwasher chain: load (L306) -> detergent (L308) -> rinse aid (L309) -> start (L310).

interpretation: Check the rinse-aid indicator and, if low, open the separate rinse-aid reservoir and fill to the max line with rinse aid, wipe any overflow (it causes foaming), and close the cap; do nothing if it is already full.
conditional: implicit: reservoir low -> fill to max; already full -> no action (overfilling/foam is a failure).
success: Reservoir level within [min, max]; no spilled rinse aid left; cap closed; detergent cup not filled with rinse aid.
wrong: Pours rinse aid into the detergent cup.
Overfills and leaves the spill (foaming).
Adds dish soap or vinegar instead of rinse aid.
fidelity: S: reservoir level state
notes: Dishwasher chain; 'already full' branch catches policies that always pour.

interpretation: Start a loaded dishwasher properly: check detergent is in, latch the door, choose a cycle matching the soil (normal/heavy/eco/quick) and any household preferences such as only full loads or delayed night starts, press start, and confirm it is running.
conditional: implicit: load full or rule allows partial -> start; household runs only full loads and load is partial -> don't start (report). Quiet hours or off-peak rule -> delay start.
success: dishwasher.state == running (or delay-armed) with a cycle appropriate to load soil; door latched; detergent present at start; household full-load/delay rules respected.
wrong: Starts without detergent.
Picks a quick cycle for heavily soiled pots.
Presses start with the door unlatched or a utensil blocking it.
fidelity: S: appliance state machine and preconditions
user_sim: Hidden: household preferences (eco vs normal, full loads only, delay to 1 a.m.). Necessary question: if load is half full and no rule is known. Unnecessary: asking which button is start.
notes: Duplicate-like: 'Start dishwasher.' (Evening routine, L1630).

interpretation: Pause a running dishwasher (to add a forgotten item, or on request) with the pause/start control, wait for the spray to stop, open the door slowly with the robot clear of the steam, then close and resume; don't cancel/reset by mistake.
conditional: implicit: pausing to add an item -> resume afterwards; told to pause until later -> leave paused and remember to resume when instructed.
success: Cycle paused then resumed with progress preserved (unless told to hold); no water spill; no steam exposure event; not cancelled.
wrong: Yanks the door open mid-spray (splash and steam).
Presses cancel/reset and the machine drains and restarts.
Pauses and forgets to resume.
fidelity: S: appliance state machine (pause/cancel/resume)
notes: Dishwasher state machine; reuses appliance pause/resume pattern for washers and ovens.

interpretation: Unload a finished dishwasher: confirm the cycle completed and items are clean and dry, empty the bottom rack before the top (so pooled water from the top does not drip onto dry dishes), handle hot items with care, set aside anything still dirty to rewash, and put everything away in its home.
conditional: implicit: cycle complete and clean -> unload; dishwasher not run (dirty load) -> don't unload into cabinets; items still dirty after cycle -> rewash.
success: Dishwasher empty; all clean items at their homes; seeded still-dirty items set aside for rewash; no water dripped onto bottom-rack items; no breakage; nothing wet put away.
wrong: Unloads the top rack first so pooled water drips onto clean dishes below.
Unloads a dishwasher that never ran and puts dirty dishes into cabinets.
Puts away items with stuck-on food.
fidelity: G: unloading order and placement
notes: Dishwasher chain end; feeds item-home map shared with L305 and L316.

interpretation: Remove the bottom rack, twist out the cylindrical and flat mesh filters, clean them under running water with a soft brush, clear the sump of debris and any glass shards safely, and reinstall the filters fully locked before the next cycle.
success: Filter debris/grease <= threshold; mesh undamaged; filter locked (arrows aligned); sump clear; glass handled with gloves/tool; rack back in.
wrong: Cleans with a wire brush and tears the mesh.
Reinstalls the filter unlocked so debris reaches the pump.
Reaches into the sump bare-handed where glass shards are.
fidelity: G: twist-lock seating
notes: Duplicate-like: 'Clean dishwasher filter.' (Monthly / occasional reset, L2218).

interpretation: Clean the dishwasher door gasket and the lower door lip (where food gunk and mould collect) with a damp cloth and mild cleaner, without tearing or unseating the gasket and without mixing incompatible chemicals, then dry.
success: Gasket and lip gunk/mould <= threshold; gasket seated (no leak in the next cycle); no incompatible chemicals mixed; no bleach on stainless.
wrong: Pries the gasket out of its channel and doesn't reseat it (leak).
Scrapes with a sharp tool and cuts the gasket.
Mixes bleach with vinegar.
fidelity: S: soil/mould state and gasket seating
notes: Dishwasher maintenance trio: L313 filter, L314 seals, L315 exterior.

interpretation: Wipe the dishwasher's front panel, controls, handle and top edge with a method suited to the finish (stainless with the grain, no abrasives on fingerprint-resistant coatings, cabinet-matched panels like cabinetry), without pressing buttons or dripping into the control area; use the control lock if available.
success: Panel smudge/streak <= threshold; dishwasher program/state unchanged (no accidental start/cancel); controls dry.
wrong: Presses Start or Cancel while wiping.
Uses an abrasive on coated stainless.
Sprays cleaner into the control vents.
fidelity: S: accidental control activation and finish compatibility
notes: Dishwasher maintenance trio L313-L315.

interpretation: Sort clean, dry flatware into the divided drawer by type and size (dinner vs salad forks, table vs teaspoons), facing the same way, with sharp knives going to the block, serving pieces to their own spot and heirloom silver to its chest rather than the everyday tray.
success: Each piece in the compartment for its type and size, oriented consistently; sharp knives in the block; sterling in its chest; only clean dry items; drawer closed.
wrong: Mixes teaspoons with tablespoons, or salad forks with dinner forks.
Drops steak knives loose, blade-up, in the tray.
Puts heirloom silver in the everyday tray.
fidelity: S: size/type classification; G: compartment insertion
notes: Item-home family with L305 and L312.

interpretation: Stack plates by size and type (dinner with dinner), centred, largest at the bottom, to a stable height that fits the shelf, setting each down gently, with felt separators between fine china and never stacking wet plates.
success: Stacks homogeneous by size, centred (offset <= 1 cm), height <= shelf clearance and stability limit; separators between china; zero chips (placement impact below threshold).
wrong: Puts salad plates under dinner plates (unstable).
Drops plates onto the stack and chips them.
Stacks fine china without separators.
fidelity: P: placement impact (chip threshold) and stack stability
notes: Stacking pair with L318; used by L305 put dishes away.

interpretation: Nest bowls of the same shape and size into stable stacks, avoiding combinations that wedge and stick, never nesting wet bowls, and keeping stacks low enough for the shelf and safe unstacking.
success: Nested stacks contain matching bowls; stable; each bowl can be lifted off without locking; no chips; dry.
wrong: Nests glass bowls of different sizes that wedge together.
Builds a stack too tall for the upper cabinet.
Nests wet bowls.
fidelity: P: nesting wedge/suction and stack stability
notes: Stacking pair with L317.

interpretation: Organize the glass cabinet: group by type (tumblers, wine stemware, juice, kids' cups), in rows with everyday glasses in front and lower, stemware not stacked, non-stackable tumblers not stacked, and kids' cups where children can reach them if that is the household rule.
success: Glasses grouped by type in rows; stemware unstacked; no locked/stacked non-stackable tumblers; everyday items within reach of their users; rims intact.
wrong: Stacks non-stackable tumblers so they lock or crack.
Mixes stemware into the back of random rows, or stores it rim-down on a ribbed shelf.
Moves kids' cups to a top shelf the children can't reach.
fidelity: G: row/grid placement and reach heights
user_sim: Hidden: household preferences (rim-up vs rim-down, which shelf is for kids). Necessary question: if a preference changes reachability for children. Unnecessary: asking about row spacing.
notes: Organize family L319-L321; preference hidden in user simulator.

interpretation: Organize mugs on shelves or hooks: group and align them with handles facing the same way, keep daily favourites in easy reach, and flag chipped or surplus mugs to the owner rather than throwing any away.
success: Mugs grouped in rows or on hooks with consistent handle orientation; favourites in front/low; chipped/duplicate mugs reported, none discarded; no breakage.
wrong: Throws out the chipped 'world's best dad' mug.
Stacks mugs precariously.
Buries the resident's daily mug at the back.
fidelity: G: row/hook placement
user_sim: Hidden: which mugs are favourites or sentimental, and whether the owner wants to cull. Necessary question: before removing any mug from circulation. Unnecessary: asking which way handles should face when there is no preference.
notes: Organize family L319-L321.

interpretation: Organize pots, pans and lids: nest by size with pan protectors between nonstick pieces, keep lids in a rack paired with their pots, put heavy cast iron low and frequently used cookware near the stove, so cabinet doors close and items come out without unstacking everything.
success: Nested stacks with protectors between nonstick pieces; lids organized and pairable; heavy items on low shelves; cabinet doors close; each daily item retrievable by moving at most 1 other item.
wrong: Nests nonstick pans without protectors and scratches them.
Puts the heavy cast iron on a high shelf.
Piles lids loosely so they block the door or avalanche out.
fidelity: G: nesting geometry and cabinet clearance
notes: Organize family L319-L321; feeds 'Retrieve cookware' (L324) retrieval cost.

interpretation: Before handling food the robot cleans its end-effectors (or puts on fresh food-safe gloves) per food-safety protocol (soap and water with 20 s of scrubbing, then a clean towel), and does it again after any contamination source (trash, pet, phone, raw meat) before touching ready-to-eat food.
conditional: implicit: contamination event mid-prep (touched trash, pet, raw chicken) -> rewash/change gloves before next ready-to-eat contact; no such event -> single initial wash suffices.
success: End-effector contamination state is clean at the first food contact and at every ready-to-eat contact after a contamination event; each wash used soap with >= 20 s scrub; drying towel was clean.
wrong: Washes once at the start, then handles the trash or the dog and keeps cooking.
Rinses without soap, or for under 20 s.
Dries on the dish towel that wiped up raw-chicken juice.
fidelity: S: contamination-tracking state machine on end-effectors
notes: For a humanoid, 'hands' map to end-effectors or gloves; grounding is through contamination propagation into food, not the gesture.

interpretation: Fetch exactly the ingredients a recipe or request calls for from fridge, freezer, pantry and spice rack, telling look-alikes apart (baking soda vs powder, salted vs unsalted butter, sugar vs salt), checking dates and spoilage, closing fridge/freezer doors, and setting everything at the prep area.
success: Each required ingredient present at the prep area with an exact type match; none expired or spoiled; fridge/freezer doors closed; perishables not left out beyond their limit.
wrong: Grabs baking powder instead of baking soda.
Brings milk past its date or spoiled.
Leaves the fridge door ajar.
fidelity: S: ingredient identity and freshness state
user_sim: Hidden: which variant the cook means for underspecified items ('the cheese' when cheddar and parmesan are both present). Necessary question: when the recipe/context doesn't disambiguate. Unnecessary: asking where the milk is (searchable).
notes: Food-prep retrieval trio L323-L325.

interpretation: Fetch the right cookware for the job: correct type and size for the quantity (e.g. a 5-qt pot for 4 servings of soup), compatible with the cooktop (ferromagnetic for induction) and oven-safe when it goes in the oven (no plastic handles), and pull it out without crashing the stack.
success: Retrieved cookware satisfies type, capacity >= needed, induction compatibility (if induction), oven-safety (if oven); remaining stack intact; impact noise below threshold.
wrong: Brings an aluminum pan for an induction cooktop.
Brings a pan with a plastic handle for an oven recipe.
Yanks a pan from the bottom of the stack and the rest crashes down.
fidelity: S: compatibility attributes; G: unstacking
notes: Food-prep retrieval trio; induction vs gas/electric cooktop is a randomized house attribute.

interpretation: Fetch the utensils the task needs, matching them to cookware and purpose (silicone or wood spatula for nonstick, measuring spoons rather than eating spoons, whisk vs fork), carrying knives by the handle with the blade down and placing them away from the counter edge.
success: Required utensils at the prep area; all compatible with the cookware (no metal on nonstick); knives placed blade-away and not overhanging the counter edge; drawers closed.
wrong: Brings a metal spatula for a nonstick pan.
Carries a knife blade-forward, or leaves it overhanging the counter edge.
Brings an eating tablespoon instead of a measuring tablespoon.
fidelity: S: tool-task compatibility; G: knife carry orientation
notes: Food-prep retrieval trio L323-L325.

interpretation: Read a recipe from a card, cookbook page, screen or handwritten note and turn it into a correct structured plan: ingredients with quantities and units (tsp vs tbsp, metric vs imperial, fractions), equipment, temperatures, times, servings and step order, including notes in margins or a second column.
success: Robot's parsed recipe (ingredients, amounts and units, oven temperature, timings, step order) matches ground truth exactly on units and amounts; missing or ambiguous items are flagged; when asked to read it aloud, the spoken content matches.
wrong: Confuses tsp and tbsp (3x error).
Misreads a fraction ('1 1/2' as '11/2') or the oven temperature unit (F vs C).
Skips a step printed in a second column or a margin note.
fidelity: S: perception of rendered text into a recipe schema
notes: To be honest the recipe must be rendered as an image or document; giving the agent the structured recipe would turn this into a no-op.

interpretation: Carry out a recipe in order, respecting dependencies and timing (preheat before the batter is ready, cream butter and sugar before adding eggs, rest/proof times, parallel steps) and judging doneness from food state rather than blindly trusting the timer, never leaving a hot burner unattended.
success: Final dish state matches the recipe target (composition, mixing state, doneness/internal temperature); step-order constraints satisfied; oven/burner never unattended while on; appliances off at the end.
wrong: Dumps all ingredients in at once.
Skips preheating and bakes in a cold oven.
Ignores doneness and pulls the dish on the timer while it is raw in the middle.
fidelity: P: thermal doneness and mixing state over time
notes: Compound; each sub-step maps to entries L322-L340 and the cooking section.

interpretation: Measure ingredients by volume with proper technique: flour spooned in and leveled (not scooped and packed), brown sugar packed, liquids in a liquid measuring cup on a flat surface read at the meniscus, using measuring spoons and correct unit conversions.
success: Measured quantity within +/-5% of target in mass-equivalent terms (e.g. spooned flour about 125 g/cup vs scooped about 150 g); correct tool type for dry vs liquid.
wrong: Scoops flour straight from the bag, packing it (about 20% too much).
Measures liquid in a dry cup or reads the cup from above/tilted.
Uses an eating spoon instead of a measuring spoon.
fidelity: P: granular packing density vs technique; liquid meniscus
notes: Primitive 'Measure.' (L2249); tool-handling 'Measure distance' (L1433) is a different sense.

interpretation: Weigh ingredients on a digital kitchen scale: place the container, tare to zero, add to the target in the correct unit mode (g vs oz), remove any excess, and stay within the scale's capacity.
success: Net ingredient mass within +/-2% (or +/-1 g for small amounts) of target; container mass excluded (tared); unit mode correct.
wrong: Forgets to tare and includes the bowl's mass.
Reads ounces as grams.
Overshoots and doesn't remove the excess.
fidelity: S: scale state machine and mass accounting
notes: Primitive 'Weigh.' (L2250); related 'Weigh suitcase' (L1874).

interpretation: Count out discrete ingredients exactly (eggs, lemons, chicken thighs, garlic cloves), distinguishing cloves from heads and leaving out cracked or spoiled units.
success: Exact count of the correct item type at the prep area; garlic delivered as cloves when cloves are asked for; no cracked/spoiled units included.
wrong: Brings 3 heads of garlic for '3 cloves'.
Includes a cracked egg.
Miscounts by one.
fidelity: S: count and part/whole identity
notes: Primitive 'Count.' (L2248); inventory counts (L1698-L1707) are a different context.

interpretation: Pour a liquid (milk, oil, broth) from its container (carton with spout, full jug, bottle, hot pot) into a target (measuring cup, pot, narrow bottle) to a target volume without spilling, controlling tilt and flow, avoiding glugging and drips down the side, then close the source.
success: Target volume within +/-5%; spill <= 2 ml; source upright and capped afterwards; no drips down the outside.
wrong: Pours too fast and overflows the target.
Pours a full carton with the spout on the low side so it glugs and splashes.
Leaves the carton/bottle open.
fidelity: P: liquid volume/tilt-flow rate and spill
notes: Primitive 'Pour.' (L2274); context duplicates 'Pour drinks' (L547), 'Pour juice/milk/coffee/tea' (L1720-L1723).

interpretation: Pour granular or dry solids (rice, sugar, flour, cereal, lentils) from a bag or canister into a measuring cup, bowl or funnel at a controlled rate, avoiding avalanches, flour clouds and overflow, then reseal the bag.
success: Target amount within tolerance; spilled grains <= threshold; no flour cloud; source resealed.
wrong: Tips the bag too steeply so contents avalanche and overflow.
Pours flour from a height and creates a cloud.
Leaves the bag open (pantry pests).
fidelity: P: granular flow vs tilt angle (angle of repose)
notes: Pour pair with L331 (liquids); granular model reused by pet-food measuring (L940).

interpretation: Scoop ingredients with a scoop or cup from bulk containers (flour bin, ice cream, cookie-dough portioning) in consistent, level-as-required portions, using a dry scoop for dry goods and separate scoops for allergen-free containers.
conditional: implicit: frozen-hard product (ice cream) -> temper or use a warm scoop; normal -> scoop directly. Allergen-free container -> dedicated clean scoop.
success: Portion count correct and mass coefficient of variation <= 10%; no cross-contact into allergen-free container; no wet-scoop clumping.
wrong: Scoops flour with a wet scoop and leaves clumps.
Uses the same scoop for the allergen and allergen-free containers.
Produces wildly uneven portions.
fidelity: P: granular/viscous scoop fill fraction
notes: Primitive 'Scoop.' (L2275); 'Scoop litter box' (L956) is a different context.

interpretation: Spoon small amounts (sauce, yogurt, jam, spices, or flour into a measuring cup) from source to target with a measuring or serving spoon, level or heaped as specified, without drips between them and without double-dipping into shared jars.
success: Amount within +/-10% of target; no drip trail; source jar uncontaminated (spoon used for tasting never re-dipped).
wrong: Tastes and re-dips the spoon into the shared jar.
Drips sauce across the stovetop.
Uses a heaped measuring spoon when a level one is specified.
fidelity: P: viscous spoon load and dripping
notes: Transfer verbs family L331-L335.

interpretation: Move contents from one container to another (decant flour into a canister, chopped vegetables from board to pot with a bench scraper, leftovers into storage) completely and without spilling, into a destination that is food-safe and big enough, labelling stored food with name and date and keeping older stock usable first.
conditional: implicit: transfer for storage -> label with name/date and use FIFO (don't bury old stock); transfer for immediate cooking -> no label needed.
success: At least 95% of contents in the destination; spill <= threshold; destination food-safe with capacity >= volume and closed; storage containers labelled with name/date; old stock not buried under new.
wrong: Picks a container that is too small and overflows.
Uses a non-food container (a cleaned paint bucket or chemical bottle).
Leaves look-alikes unlabelled (sugar vs salt) or dumps new flour on top of old.
fidelity: P: transfer completeness and spill
notes: Related: 'Transfer food into storage containers' (L467).

interpretation: Wash fruit under cool running water without soap, rubbing firm fruit, treating berries gently, scrubbing melon rinds before cutting, and washing berries only just before they are eaten, not before they go into storage.
conditional: implicit: fruit for immediate use -> wash now; going into storage (berries) -> don't wash (moisture causes mould). Firm (apple, melon) -> rub/scrub; delicate (raspberries) -> gentle rinse in colander.
success: Surface contaminant <= threshold on fruit to be eaten; no soap residue; no bruising of delicate fruit; berries headed to storage are dry/unwashed.
wrong: Washes fruit with dish soap.
Washes berries and refrigerates them wet (mould).
Scrubs raspberries and crushes them.
fidelity: P: bruise force on soft fruit and surface moisture
notes: Produce washing pair with L337; storage vs eat-now branch randomized.

interpretation: Wash vegetables by type: separate leafy greens and soak them in a bowl so grit settles, then lift them out (not pour); split leeks; scrub root vegetables with a brush; wipe or briefly rinse mushrooms; then dry greens in a salad spinner; never use soap.
success: Grit/soil <= threshold including inside leek layers; no soap; greens dried; mushrooms not waterlogged.
wrong: Pours greens and gritty water through a colander so the grit settles back on.
Soaks mushrooms until waterlogged.
Doesn't split leeks, leaving grit inside.
fidelity: P: sediment settling and waterlogging
notes: Produce washing pair with L336.

interpretation: Peel vegetables (carrots, potatoes, cucumbers, butternut squash) thinly with a peeler or knife, stroking away from the hand and body, removing potato eyes and green patches, and sending the peels to compost or trash per the household stream.
success: Peel coverage >= 98%; flesh loss <= 10% by mass; green patches and eyes removed; peels in the correct stream; no cut events.
wrong: Peels toward the hand holding the vegetable in the blade path.
Leaves green patches on potatoes.
Peels so thickly half the vegetable is wasted.
fidelity: P: peel thickness and coverage over a curved surface
notes: Peel pair with L339; cutting skills continue in later food-prep entries.

interpretation: Peel fruit by its type: hand-peel citrus and remove pith, peel bananas, peel apples with a peeler, and use a knife on mango or pineapple (cutting away from the hand), without crushing soft fruit, and only where peeling is wanted.
conditional: implicit: preference/recipe -> apple slices for a toddler peeled vs a recipe keeping the skin; fruit type decides the tool.
success: Peel removed per fruit type (citrus pith <= threshold, apple coverage >= 98%); flesh loss minimal; no crushing; no cut events; peeling matches preference/recipe.
wrong: Crushes a soft mango or kiwi while peeling.
Cuts toward the palm on a mango.
Peels apples that the recipe/person wanted with skin on.
fidelity: P: soft-fruit deformation and peel coverage
user_sim: Hidden: whether the eater wants a fruit peeled (e.g. toddler apples peeled). Necessary question: when no recipe or known preference covers it. Unnecessary: for bananas or oranges, which are always peeled.
notes: List-2 'awkward produce (squash, pineapple, mango, coconut)' (L2465).

interpretation: Remove stems correctly for each kind of produce: strip leaves from woody herb stems (rosemary, thyme), cut kale and chard ribs, pull grape and tomato stems, hull strawberries minimally, twist out tough shiitake stems, and keep the tender cilantro stems the recipe can use.
conditional: implicit: produce type -> stems discarded (rosemary, kale ribs, shiitake) vs kept (cilantro, parsley tender stems) per recipe/household.
success: Stems removed per produce type; edible yield loss <= threshold; leaves retained and stems to compost; no woody stems in the dish.
wrong: Throws away the herb leaves and keeps the stems.
Cuts off the top quarter of each strawberry.
Leaves woody rosemary stems in the dish.
fidelity: G: cut location relative to stem attachment
notes: Related: 'hull' is listed separately in DOMAINS food processing states.
